AETHERVEIL — UNIFIED MASTER EXECUTION DIRECTIVE + EXPANSION
READ THIS BEFORE THE ORIGINAL MASTER SPECIFICATION BELOW
======================================================================

This file combines the user's original Aetherveil Ultimate RPG Master Prompt with the newer, explicit requirements for a much larger integrated cyberpunk RPG + driving + aviation game. The original master specification is retained in full after this directive. Treat this directive as the current top-level priority where newer requirements extend or clarify the original. Do not discard the original lore, systems, character requirements, existing project protections, or details just because this new directive is shorter.

PROJECT IDENTITY
AETHERVEIL is one cohesive, original, premium-quality, third-person open-world anime action RPG, life simulation, cyberpunk city adventure, high-speed driving game, aircraft/aviation game, and cosmic mystery. It is not a set of disconnected modes. The player can move naturally between walking, parkour, combat, social life, cars, motorcycles, boats, aircraft, futuristic transport, story missions, exploration, and cosmic/secret-realm content while retaining the same character, world state, story flags, inventory, relationships, vehicle ownership, progression, and saves.

PRIMARY TARGET
The intended long-term quality bar is a premium modern AAA-style experience: the visual ambition and character appeal of high-end anime action RPGs such as Wuthering Waves; the dense, moody, neon-soaked urban atmosphere and technological layering associated with cyberpunk fiction; and the scale, vehicle variety, handling, road exploration, vehicle customisation and event density of major open-world driving games such as Forza Horizon. These are broad quality/genre references only. Aetherveil must have original IP, characters, story, factions, world layout, vehicle silhouettes, UI, logos, music, and assets. Never copy distinctive protected assets or designs from existing games.

KEY ART REFERENCE — HIGHEST-PRIORITY ART-DIRECTION INPUT
The user will provide key art reference image(s) with this prompt. Inspect them carefully before making art-direction decisions. Treat them as the primary visual north star for Aetherveil's palette, lighting, architecture, silhouette language, atmosphere, scale, composition, fashion, technology, and mood. Extract a written visual bible from the reference: palette; materials; architectural motifs; neon density; light sources; sky/cosmic elements; environmental scale; character styling; vehicle styling; fog/weather; contrast; and camera/composition. Match the broad visual language consistently across environments, characters, vehicles, aircraft, UI, VFX, loading screens, cinematics, promotional screenshots and key locations. Do not simply paste the key art into the game, create a flat 2D scene, or assume the image itself is a finished asset. Convert the reference into real 3D production decisions and in-engine scenes. If a reference conflicts with an old generic visual description, prefer the user's supplied key art for overall art direction while preserving Aetherveil's original lore and functional systems.

NON-NEGOTIABLE GAME REQUIREMENTS
- This must be a real playable 3D game, not a webpage, menu mockup, screenshot, pitch, concept scene, or collection of disconnected demos.
- Do not intentionally make the world low-poly, toy-like, flat, generic, or prototype-looking. Use the best available game-ready assets and rendering features the target hardware/engine can actually support.
- Do not claim AAA quality has been achieved just because the prompt asks for it. Build, run, test, inspect and improve the real project; report verified results and genuine blockers.
- Do not stop after writing a plan. Start implementing in the actual project through available tools and continue autonomously across small, testable milestones.
- Do not ask the user to decide routine implementation details already specified here or in the original master prompt. Make sound choices and proceed.
- Do not use fake buttons, nonfunctional menu entries, placeholder systems presented as complete, static characters pretending to be NPCs, empty roads pretending to be a driving game, or parked vehicle meshes presented as a complete vehicle system.
- Do not remove, reset, or rewrite the existing project. Inspect and reuse existing work first. Preserve working features and assets, current save data, world streaming, level/World Partition structure, project settings, plugins, input, and existing Aetherveil systems unless a specific verified reason requires a carefully tested change.

INTEGRATED GAME PILLARS
1. ANIME ACTION RPG: original playable characters, third-person movement, responsive combat, character switching, weapons, abilities, bosses, progression, equipment, exploration, quests, cinematics, dialogue, character biographies, relationships and story choices.
2. LIFE SIMULATION: school/campus, classes and clubs, cafes, restaurants, shopping, entertainment, home/housing, interiors, daily routines, social activities, festivals, dates, events, clothing, character customisation, phone/apps, schedules, and world activities. Social and life-sim features are part of the same world and affect the story and NPCs.
3. CYBERPUNK MEGACITY: dense futuristic city with immense layered skyscrapers, neon signage, holograms, elevated roads, maglev transit, corporate towers, slums/back alleys, markets, nightlife, industrial zones, docks, transit hubs, rooftops, underground networks, secret labs, security forces, cybernetic tech, digital systems, augmented interfaces, and strong contrasts between wealthy and neglected districts. Use neon with restraint and purpose; not every surface should glow. The city must feel lived-in, vertically explorable, navigable, and populated.
4. OPEN-WORLD DRIVING: driving is a major pillar, not an occasional minigame. Build road networks, highways, mountain routes, coastal roads, tunnels, elevated expressways, underground routes, industrial roads, city streets, scenic routes, off-road routes, race circuits, drift zones, time trials, delivery missions, pursuits, stunt events, exploration drives, and vehicle-related story missions.
5. AVIATION AND FLIGHT: include functional aircraft and planes as part of the world. Aircraft are not just background props. Provide flyable aircraft with real controls, flight model, takeoff/landing, throttle, pitch/roll/yaw, braking, camera options, landing gear where applicable, cockpit/external view where supported, damage, repair, storage, and flight missions. Create airports, airfields, helipads, VTOL pads, hangars, air traffic, restricted zones, air races, aerial exploration, rescue/cargo/transport missions, and high-altitude points of interest. Make aviation fit the world's technology and fiction.
6. COSMIC / SECRET-REALM EXPLORATION: spaceports, orbital structures, stations, floating cities/islands, alien environments, planets/moons in the sky, cosmic anomalies, dimensional portals, ruins, hidden realms, research facilities and unusual traversal. These are connected to city life, faction plots, driving/flight and the central mystery.
7. COLLECTING AND CUSTOMISATION: a broad collection-driven game with original characters, cars, bikes, boats, aircraft, clothing, equipment, home decorations and other unlockables. Unlock primarily through gameplay, story, exploration, achievements, events, contracts, reputation and purchases using in-game currency. Do not add paid gambling, loot boxes, or forced real-money mechanics.

WORLD AND DISTRICT DESIGN
Build a large, dense, coherent world that expands in stages. Include a central neon megacity, downtown/skyscraper district, corporate/financial district, residential neighbourhoods, school/campus, shopping streets, entertainment/nightlife district, arcades, cafes, restaurants, gyms, hospitals, police/security facilities, industrial/factory district, harbour and marina, beaches, parks, forests, mountains, desert or wasteland where suitable, old-city/Sakura-style district if compatible with key art, underground facilities, subway/maglev network, sewers/tunnels, construction sites, remote islands, airport, aviation base, spaceport, orbital station, hidden labs, secret bases, ancient ruins, supernatural spaces, pocket dimensions and cosmic environments. Each district needs a distinctive architecture language, residents, traffic, activities, music, lighting, weather, hazards, missions, secrets and faction presence.

The world must be vertical and traversable: ground level, interiors, balconies, elevated walkways, rooftops, transit platforms, skybridges, aerial routes, underground areas and flyable airspace. Avoid a giant empty map. Prioritise density, scale, sightlines, landmarks, discoverability and meaningful activities. Use streaming and world partitioning intelligently; do not force the entire world and all vehicle/character assets into memory simultaneously.

MASSIVE VEHICLE LIBRARY — MAJOR REQUIREMENT
Build a large, organised, expandable vehicle collection, not just one car. Long-term target: at least 100 distinct, original, properly catalogued vehicle variants across all categories, with a scalable asset/data architecture so the collection can grow well beyond that. This is a long-term content target, not permission to flood the map with low-quality duplicates. Each listed vehicle must have a unique identity, coherent model/silhouette, category, name, visual specification, acquisition method, stats, supported functions, and asset status. Build high-quality exemplar vehicles first, prove the complete gameplay loop, then expand the catalogue systematically. Do not claim a catalogue entry is playable if only its thumbnail/data record exists.

VEHICLE CATEGORIES — INCLUDE ALL APPROPRIATE CATEGORIES
A. Road cars: hypercars, supercars, sports coupes, grand tourers, sedans, luxury limousines, executive cars, hatchbacks, compacts, wagons, muscle-inspired cars, rally cars, off-roaders, SUVs, pickups, utility vehicles, classic/retro-futuristic cars, electric performance cars, autonomous taxis, police/security cars, emergency response vehicles, ambulances, fire/rescue vehicles, delivery vans, cargo trucks, semis/tractor-trailers, buses, minibuses, shuttles, service vehicles, racing prototypes, drift builds, drag builds, time-attack cars, endurance/rally variants and heavily modified street builds.
B. Motorcycles and two-wheelers: sport bikes, superbikes, streetfighters, touring bikes, cruisers, off-road/enduro bikes, motocross bikes, electric bikes, cyberpunk hoverbikes, delivery bikes, scooters and specialised racing variants.
C. Futuristic/cyberpunk transport: hovercars, anti-gravity cars, maglev commuter pods, autonomous shuttles, personal air vehicles, VTOL road/air hybrids, magnetic rail vehicles, monorail trains, maglev trains, freight trains and specialised corporate/security vehicles.
D. Watercraft: speedboats, yachts, personal watercraft, patrol boats, ferries, cargo vessels and futuristic hydrofoils/submersible craft if compatible with the world.
E. Helicopters and rotorcraft: civilian, medical/rescue, cargo, police/security, corporate transport, heavy-lift and futuristic tiltrotor variants.
F. Fixed-wing aircraft and PLANES: small propeller aircraft, trainers, private jets, business jets, passenger airliners, cargo aircraft, seaplanes, bush/STOL aircraft, aerobatic aircraft, air-racing aircraft, military-inspired fictional aircraft, futuristic electric planes, supersonic futuristic craft, heavy cargo planes, reconnaissance aircraft and original sci-fi atmospheric aircraft. Include a sensible mixture of grounded conventional aviation and advanced fictional technology.
G. VTOL and advanced aircraft: tiltrotors, vertical-lift transports, flying taxis, personal air vehicles, rescue aircraft, cargo VTOLs, futuristic interceptors and advanced experimental craft.
H. Space vehicles: orbital shuttles, crew transports, cargo shuttles, landing craft, exploration craft, small spacecraft and other appropriate original vehicles for spaceport/orbital content. Space flight is a separate advanced milestone if the current project does not yet support it; do not fake space flight with a static backdrop.

VEHICLE QUALITY AND GAMEPLAY
- Every vehicle category must have the correct driving/flying/water/space handling model rather than all vehicles sharing identical physics.
- Road vehicles need acceleration, braking, steering, suspension, grip, traction, drift behaviour where relevant, collisions, damage, repair, reverse, lights, brake lights, indicators where applicable, horn, sound, engine/electric motor response, wheel rotation, camera modes, vehicle entry/exit, passenger seating where supported, and consistent collision/scale.
- Aircraft need functional flight input, takeoff/landing, speed/stall constraints appropriate to type, pitch/roll/yaw, throttle, camera and landing gear where applicable. Do not label a car with wings a flyable plane unless the flight loop works.
- Provide touch-friendly controls where mobile/browser support is relevant and keyboard/controller support for the main PC game. Ensure the controls are rebindable if the existing architecture supports it.
- Add AI traffic and sensible road navigation, traffic lights/signals where appropriate, pedestrian safety behaviours, police/emergency response, races, pursuits, vehicle challenges, aerial traffic/air routes where feasible, and vehicle spawning/streaming that avoids congestion and memory spikes.
- Build a vehicle garage/showroom with 3D rotation, vehicle stats, ownership, locked/unlocked status, category filters, search, favourites, sorting, comparison, selection, storage, upgrades, tuning, paint, wraps, decals, wheels, suspension, body kits, lights, interior options, performance upgrades and saved configurations where appropriate.
- Use an original fictional manufacturer ecosystem: distinct brands, model families, design languages, price tiers, rarity tiers if useful, lore, dealership/showroom locations, race teams, underground tuners, aircraft manufacturers and corporate fleets. Do not copy real brand logos or exact protected car designs. Broad vehicle class references are allowed; final designs must be original.
- Create a large catalogue UI that remains useful as the library grows: search, filters, vehicle thumbnails, clear data assets, consistent naming, preview scene, acquisition hints, handling class and progression. Separate cataloguing from whether an asset is actually implemented and tested.
- Every vehicle that is represented as drivable/flyable must have an implemented control/physics loop, appropriate collision, camera, audio, entry/exit/spawn logic, save/ownership integration and test. Background traffic vehicles may be simpler, but label and use them honestly.

DRIVING-GAME CONTENT
Include a substantial activity ecosystem: street races, legal race events, circuit racing, point-to-point road races, sprint events, time trials, drift zones, speed traps, speed cameras, stunt jumps, skill chains, off-road rallies, endurance races, highway runs, delivery contracts, taxi/transport missions, emergency response, vehicle recovery, courier races, convoy escorts, pursuit escapes, aerial races and flight challenges. The game should reward exploration and mastery, not just raw speed. Vehicles must be useful in free roam and story missions. Ensure missions are integrated with the RPG, NPCs, factions and world state.

CYBERPUNK VISUAL AND SYSTEMS DIRECTION
The main city should feel unmistakably cyberpunk while remaining original to Aetherveil and consistent with the supplied key art: towering layered megastructures, illuminated signs, holographic ads, LED strips, animated signage, dense cables and infrastructure, rainy reflective streets where appropriate, elevated transit, neon-lit markets, narrow alleys, corporate security, cybernetic augmentation, AR overlays, futuristic public transport, vending machines, kiosks, data terminals, surveillance systems, black-market tech, drones, nightlife, rooftop gardens, giant digital billboards, industrial smog, atmospheric fog and dramatic skyline composition. Balance saturated neon with darkness, natural light, warm interiors, muted surfaces, and readable silhouettes. Do not make every scene uniformly purple/cyan or excessively glowy. Add interactive elements where feasible: doors, terminals, shops, lifts, transit, security gates, advertisements, services, vendors, missions, hidden entrances and world events.

CHARACTERS, NPCS AND SOCIAL SYSTEMS
Preserve and expand the original master prompt's fully customisable player character, playable roster, relationships, dating/affinity, dialogue, NPC routines, school/campus life, factions, story, combat and progression. Maintain a roughly balanced playable roster across male and female characters, with genuinely distinct designs, personalities, voices, animation identities and gameplay roles. Character unlocks should be fair and earned through story, quests, exploration, achievements, reputation and events, not paid random loot boxes. NPCs must have homes, destinations, schedules, jobs, social ties, dialogue context, needs or routines as appropriate, and reactions to location, time, weather, quests, player actions, faction standing, relationships and world events. Aircraft pilots, mechanics, racers, dealers, couriers, students, teachers, scientists, doctors, investigators, gang/faction members, corporate staff, transport workers and ordinary citizens should make the city feel inhabited.

STORY AND LORE INTEGRATION
Preserve Aetherveil's original futuristic cosmic anime setting and mystery. The cyberpunk megacity must not erase the cosmic/supernatural layer; integrate it into the central mystery. Corporate power, faction politics, technology, hidden research, strange anomalies, secret realms, orbital structures and aviation/vehicle industries should connect to the main plot. Let the player choose how to spend time: story, exploration, relationships, school/life sim, combat, driving, aviation, collection, customisation, racing, trade, discovery or world events. Do not force a single gameplay loop.

PROGRESSION AND ECONOMY
Use one coherent save and progression model. Track player character and customisation, playable character roster, story chapters, quest flags, relationship values, faction reputation, inventory, equipment, credits/currency, owned vehicles, vehicle tuning and cosmetics, garages/hangars, unlocked regions, discovered landmarks, race records, flight records, collectibles and achievements. Provide meaningful ways to earn money and unlock content through activities. Avoid pay-to-win and gambling. Ensure rewards, unlocks and mission outcomes persist after save/load.

UI / PRESENTATION / KEY ART
Create a premium title screen and main menu with an original logo, background scene, subtle animated elements, audio, responsive controls, settings, accessibility options, save slots where appropriate and a smooth transition into a cinematic intro after Start/New Game. The opening cinematic must transition seamlessly into actual gameplay and the first quest, not end at a static menu. Include high-quality loading screens with rotating original key art, lore snippets, character/vehicle facts and progress feedback. Build clean, stylish interfaces for map, quests, phone, dialogue, inventory, character roster, character creator, wardrobe, relationships, faction reputation, vehicle collection, garage, race events, aircraft hangar, flight planning, shops, settings, save/load and codex. UI must be functional and connected to actual data. Do not use screenshots as fake live gameplay.

AUDIO AND CINEMATICS
Use the existing audio pipeline if available. Use Kokoro for original NPC voice lines/voices and ACE-Step for original music across exploration, city districts, school/cafe, nightlife, racing, vehicle interiors, aircraft, combat, bosses, emotional scenes, story, menus and events. Build ambient layers for traffic, pedestrians, announcements, trains, aircraft, hangars, ocean, wind, rain, machinery, city nights and interiors. Music and dialogue must be original and legally usable. Generate/cache assets ahead of gameplay when possible. Add cinematic cameras, character performances, transitions, environmental storytelling, vehicle/aircraft reveal scenes and story triggers.

UNREAL ENGINE AND TOOL EXECUTION
The existing Aetherveil project is Unreal Engine 5.8. Treat the current project and its files as authoritative. Use the actual connected tools that are available rather than pretending tools exist. Where configured and available, use Unreal MCP/AllToolsets for levels, Actors, Blueprints, materials, gameplay, UI, lighting, Niagara, PCG, Enhanced Input, GAS, StateTree, testing, screenshots and packaging; use VibeUE/Vibe3D for supported Unreal and mesh operations; use FunPlayMCP for capabilities it exposes; use mymeshy for generating original game-ready assets; use Kokoro for voices; ACE-Step for music; and Ollama/Qwen or another configured model for local reasoning where appropriate. Do not waste time retrying a missing plugin or unavailable tool indefinitely: identify the blocker, use an available supported alternative, and continue. Do not assume a tool is installed merely because this prompt names it.

ASSET PIPELINE
Before generating an asset, inspect existing project assets and the user's supplied assets. Reuse good assets; do not create duplicates blindly. For missing assets, generate original assets with the best available asset generator, export an Unreal-compatible result, import it, inspect/refine it, set materials/textures, collision, rigging/animation, LODs or Nanite as appropriate, create an Actor/Blueprint/data asset/system integration, place or register it, and test it in game. Maintain an asset manifest that records name, category, source, license/permission status where relevant, import path, quality state, gameplay state, dependencies and verification. Avoid assets that look visibly mismatched to the key art. Do not use copyrighted characters, franchise assets, vehicle logos, music or distinctive protected designs.

AUTONOMOUS BUILD LOOP — NEVER STOP AFTER A PLAN
Operate continuously using:
INSPECT → PRIORITISE → PLAN → IMPLEMENT → SAVE → COMPILE → LAUNCH → TEST → FIX → VERIFY → UPDATE PROGRESS → CONTINUE.
Inspect the project, project settings, existing levels, character/NPC Blueprints, UI, save system, input mappings, plugins, streaming and assets before major changes. Make safe, incremental edits. Save automatically where authorised by the user's existing instructions. Compile and test after each meaningful stage. Keep a persistent progress file such as AETHERVEIL_PROGRESS.md with completed work, changed files/assets, build status, test results, known defects, next tasks and blockers. Do not claim tests passed unless actually run. Do not stop just because one tool call fails or the editor crashes; preserve progress, recover if possible, identify the actual cause, and resume from the last verified checkpoint.

BUILD PHASING — EXPAND THE SAME GAME
PHASE 0: inspect current project and key art; create the visual bible, dependency map and progress ledger; preserve existing systems.
PHASE 1: stabilise launch flow, main menu, cinematic intro, player spawn, camera, input, save/load and first quest; ensure a complete playable loop.
PHASE 2: create one premium cyberpunk city district with a functional road network, pedestrians, traffic, enterable key interiors, NPCs, lighting, weather, audio and vertical traversal.
PHASE 3: deliver one polished original car and one motorcycle with full vehicle entry/exit, handling, cameras, sounds, damage/repair, garage ownership and one working race/mission. Deliver this as a real playable loop, not a static vehicle showcase.
PHASE 4: implement the shared RPG loop: combat, quest progression, dialogue, relationship/faction flags, inventory, rewards and persistent saves.
PHASE 5: implement garage/catalogue architecture, vehicle customisation and a pipeline for the 100+ original vehicle target. Expand by coherent vehicle families and test each category.
PHASE 6: add flyable helicopter/VTOL and a first fixed-wing plane; implement flight model, takeoff/landing, hangar, ownership and a complete flight mission before expanding the aircraft library.
PHASE 7: expand driving events, vehicle types, traffic, police/faction pursuits, road districts, airports, airfields, aviation missions, watercraft and other transport.
PHASE 8: expand character roster, school/life sim, housing, interiors, shops, festivals, relationships, factions, secrets, side quests and story chapters.
PHASE 9: expand the world to additional districts, outskirts, wilderness, harbour, mountains, hidden realms, cosmic locations, spaceports and orbital areas as architecture allows.
PHASE 10: polish animation, VFX, lighting, materials, audio, UI, cinematics, world density, vehicle audio, flight audio, streaming, accessibility, performance, save integrity and packaging.
PHASE 11: run full integration regression tests and capture genuine in-engine screenshots showing actual gameplay. Do not fake screenshots or claim incomplete features are complete.

Do not interpret phases as permission to stop after any phase. Complete the first playable slice, then keep expanding autonomously. If time/tool/compute limits prevent full completion in one session, leave a persistent accurate progress file and resume from it rather than restarting or falsely claiming completion.

QUALITY GATES
Before marking any district complete, inspect scale, proportions, materials, lighting, palette, architecture, roads, traffic, vegetation, signage, props, NPCs, vehicles, VFX, collision, traversal, streaming, navigation, audio, secrets and frame stability. Remove floating objects, clipping, broken materials, duplicate clutter, mismatched assets and obvious placeholder geometry. Before marking any vehicle complete, test spawn, entry, exit, control, acceleration/throttle, steering/flight response, braking, camera, collision, sound, repair, garage/hangar ownership and save/load. Before marking any mission complete, test start, objectives, failure/success, rewards, state changes, save/load and repeat/replay behaviour where appropriate. Before marking UI complete, test every interactive control against real game state.

PERFORMANCE AND TECHNICAL QUALITY
Use Unreal Engine 5.8 features appropriately, including Nanite, Lumen, World Partition/level streaming, PCG, Niagara, LODs, culling, efficient materials, asset bundles and asynchronous loading where appropriate. Do not blindly maximise polygon counts or texture resolutions. Balance visual fidelity, memory, loading time, CPU/GPU load and world density. Use scalable graphics settings and preserve existing settings. Do not compromise the entire project to make one screenshot look good. Treat vehicles, aircraft, crowds and city density as streaming and LOD systems, not as hundreds of always-loaded actors.

FINAL REPORTING RULES
At each checkpoint, report briefly and accurately: what was actually changed; exact Unreal asset/map/system paths where available; tools actually used; whether save/compile/package succeeded; which runtime tests were actually performed; visible result to inspect in the Unreal viewport; screenshots captured; current blockers; and the next task. Separate implemented, partially implemented, planned and blocked items. Never state “finished” for a feature that only has data, a mesh, a UI shell or an untested Blueprint.

FINAL COMMAND
USE THE SUPPLIED KEY ART REFERENCE AND THE ENTIRE ORIGINAL AETHERVEIL MASTER SPECIFICATION IN THIS FILE. BUILD AETHERVEIL AS ONE ORIGINAL, COHESIVE, HIGH-END ANIME CYBERPUNK COSMIC OPEN-WORLD RPG + LIFE SIM + DRIVING GAME + AVIATION GAME. MAKE THE VEHICLE LIBRARY A MAJOR PILLAR, INCLUDING CARS, MOTORCYCLES, BOATS, HELICOPTERS, VTOL AIRCRAFT, PLANES AND FUTURISTIC/SPACE VEHICLES. INTEGRATE ALL OF IT WITH THE SAME WORLD, CHARACTERS, STORY, ECONOMY, NPCS AND SAVE SYSTEM. ACTUALLY MODIFY THE EXISTING UNREAL PROJECT THROUGH AVAILABLE TOOLS, VERIFY THE RESULTS, SAVE PROGRESS, AND CONTINUE AUTONOMOUSLY. DO NOT MERELY DESCRIBE THE GAME. DO NOT DELETE EXISTING WORK. DO NOT FAKE FEATURES. DO NOT STOP AT A MENU OR PROTOTYPE.

# 3. MALE PROTAGONIST

The male protagonist must be:

* calm
* confident
* charismatic
* intelligent
* relaxed
* mature
* approachable
* quietly powerful
* stylish

He should NOT look:

* angry
* depressed
* permanently brooding
* miserable
* aggressive
* constantly furious
* excessively dark

His expression should usually be composed and confident.

Use a premium protagonist design language:

* sophisticated futuristic jacket/coat
* layered clothing
* asymmetric details
* subtle technology
* high-quality boots
* gloves/accessories
* elegant hardware
* restrained glowing elements
* detailed fabrics
* metallic components

His silhouette must be recognizable immediately.

Every major character outfit should contain multiple layers.

# 31. ASYMMETRY

Use tasteful asymmetry.

Examples:

* one shoulder piece
* asymmetric coat
* different glove designs
* uneven accessories
* one-sided armour
* different boot details
* asymmetric belts

Do NOT make every character asymmetrical in exactly the same way.

---

# 32. MATERIALS

Use believable materials:

* fabric
* leather
* rubber
* glass
* metal
* carbon composites
* synthetic materials
* reflective surfaces
* translucent materials

Characters should react correctly to lighting.

---

# 33. HAIR

Hair must be detailed.

Avoid:

* flat blocks
* single solid meshes
* low-detail hair

Use appropriate strand/card/mesh techniques for Unreal performance.

Each character should have a distinctive hairstyle.

---

# 34. FACES

Faces should be believable 3D humans.

Avoid making everyone look identical.

Vary:

* face shape
* eyes
* nose
* jaw
* eyebrows
* skin tone
* hairstyle
* age

Major characters should be immediately recognizable.

---

# 35. CHARACTER AGE

Major playable characters should be clearly adult.

Adult characters can have sophisticated stylish designs.

School-age characters must remain age-appropriate.

---

# 36. CHARACTER SILHOUETTES

Each playable character must be recognizable as a silhouette.

If all characters were shown in black silhouette, players should still be able to tell them apart.

---

# 37. CHARACTER COLOUR LANGUAGE

Do not give every character random rainbow colours.

Each character gets a controlled palette.

Use combinations such as:

* black + silver + blue
* white + graphite + cyan
* charcoal + violet
* cream + gold
* dark green + silver
* navy + white
* burgundy + black
* grey + turquoise

But create individual palettes.

---

# 38. WEAPONS

Each playable character should have a visually appropriate weapon.

Weapons should:

* match the character
* have detailed geometry
* use PBR materials
* have unique silhouettes
* have subtle technology
* integrate with animations

---

# 39. VFX IDENTITY

Every playable character should have unique visual effects.

Effects should communicate:

* element/ability
* character personality
* combat role

Avoid copying another game's exact VFX.

---

# 40. ANIMATION IDENTITY

Characters should not all move identically.

Give them different:

* idle poses
* walking styles
* attack rhythms
* dodge animations
* combat stances
* victory animations

Personality should appear through animation.

---

* relationships
* memory

* locations
* routines

# 45. FINAL QUALITY STANDARD

The cast must look like it belongs in the same premium game.

The goal is:

**ORIGINAL NOVA CHARACTERS**

with the sophistication, detail and fashion-conscious design language of premium modern action RPGs.

NOT:

* generic AI characters
* low-poly characters
* random clothing
* identical faces
* anime drawings
* flat illustrations
* placeholder mannequins

Every major character should look intentionally designed.

# 46. 3D ASSET REQUIREMENT

The final characters must be REAL 3D assets.

Required where possible:

* Skeletal Mesh
* Skeleton
* Physics Asset
* Materials
* Textures
* LODs
* Collision
* Animation Blueprint
* Rig
* Clothing meshes
* Weapon meshes

They must be usable in Unreal Engine.

# 48. FINAL CAST GOAL

Nova should eventually have a cast where players can say:

"I recognize that character immediately."

because every character has:

* unique silhouette
* unique face
* unique outfit
* unique personality
* unique combat identity
* unique story
* unique animations
* unique visual effects

Build the roster as a cohesive universe rather than a collection of random characters.

# NOVA — COMPLETE ORIGINAL CHARACTER CAST
# NOVA — MASSIVE STORY-DRIVEN CAST + PERSONALITY-BASED CHARACTER DESIGN

Expand the Nova cast substantially.

Do not create random characters simply to increase the number.

Every important character must exist for a reason within the story, world, factions, quests, locations or gameplay.

The cast should feel like a real population of a massive futuristic world.

# 1. STORY-FIRST CHARACTER DESIGN

Every major character must have a PURPOSE.

For every character determine:

* name
* age category
* personality
* occupation
* faction
* home/location
* relationships
* story purpose
* quests
* motivations
* fears
* goals
* secrets
* abilities
* combat role if playable
* clothing style
* hairstyle
* accessories
* weapon/equipment
* visual effects
* daily schedule

Do not create a character before determining why they belong in Nova.

---

# 2. STORY CONNECTION

Characters must connect to the existing Nova storyline.

Create characters associated with:

## THE PROTAGONISTS

Friends, rivals, mentors, allies, enemies and mysterious figures connected to the protagonists.

## THE CITY

People who actually make the city function.

## THE SCHOOL

Students, teachers, staff, researchers and important story figures.

## THE CAFE

Owner, workers, regular customers, suppliers and recurring characters.

## RESEARCH ORGANIZATIONS

Scientists, directors, engineers, technicians and security.

## CITY SECURITY

Officers, commanders, investigators and specialists.

## ORBITAL SOCIETY

Pilots, engineers, researchers, station workers and explorers.

## UNDERGROUND NETWORK

Hackers, smugglers, informants, fixers and mysterious contacts.

## EXPLORER GROUPS

Scouts, researchers, adventurers and guides.

## COSMIC ANOMALY STORY

Researchers, witnesses, survivors, investigators and people affected by anomalies.

---

# 3. CHARACTER RELATIONSHIP WEB

Do not make characters exist independently.

Build relationships between them.

Examples:

Character A knows Character B.

Character B dislikes Character C.

Character C works for Faction X.

Character D secretly knows information about Character A.

Character E is connected to the protagonist's past.

Character F is a rival.

Character G is a mentor.

Character H becomes an ally after a quest.

Character I betrays the group.

Character J has information needed to unlock a hidden location.

Relationships should influence:

* dialogue
* quests
* schedules
* story flags
* missions
* character unlocks
* combat
* future conversations

---

# 4. PERSONALITY-FIRST DESIGN

THIS IS EXTREMELY IMPORTANT.

Do NOT design the clothing first.

First determine the character's personality.

Then design the character around that personality.

A:

calm scientist

should NOT dress like

a reckless street fighter.

A:

formal executive

should NOT dress like

a mechanic.

A:

rebellious hacker

should NOT dress like

a security officer.

A:

quiet explorer

should NOT dress like

a celebrity.

Clothing must communicate personality.

---

# 5. PERSONALITY → CLOTHING SYSTEM

For every character ask:

WHAT WOULD THIS PERSON ACTUALLY CHOOSE TO WEAR?

Consider:

* personality
* occupation
* social status
* faction
* hobbies
* environment
* combat role
* age
* lifestyle
* cultural influences
* practicality

Then design the outfit.

* Homes
* Jobs
* Schedules
* Destinations
* Routines
* Relationships
* Activities

NPCs can:

* Travel

* Shop

* Go to school
* Go home
* Sleep

* Commute

Different NPCs should appear at different times.

# 11. NPC REACTIONS

If the player:

* Causes destruction
* Saves someone
* Starts an event
* Gets chased
* Fights a boss

Possible reactions:

* Run away
* Record the event
* Call authorities
* Cheer
* Panic
* Take photos
* Talk about it later
* Follow the player
* Help
* Become suspicious

* Doors

# 13. ENVIRONMENTAL COMBAT

THIS IS A MAJOR FEATURE.

The environment itself is a weapon.

Allow the player to use:

* Chairs
* Tables
* Signs
* Bins
* Pipes
* Poles
* Street objects
* Tools
* Objects from shops
* Environmental debris
* Vehicles where appropriate

Objects can be:

* Picked up
* Thrown
* Slammed
* Used in finishers
* Used to knock enemies down
* Used against groups

Do not make combat happen in an isolated arena.

Make the CITY part of the combat.

---

# 14. ENEMY WEAPON SYSTEM

Enemies can carry weapons.

During combat:

* Disarm enemies
* Grab enemy weapons
* Temporarily use enemy weapons
* Throw enemy weapons
* Use different fighting styles

Make combat improvisational.

The player should be encouraged to use whatever is nearby.

---

# 15. PHYSICS-BASED COMBAT

Use physics wherever appropriate.

Enemies can:

* Fall
* Stagger
* Knock into objects
* Crash into vehicles
* Break through objects
* Be launched
* Be thrown
* Be slammed into walls

Make combat feel physical.

---

# 16. FAST ACTION COMBAT

Build responsive real-time combat.

Include:

* Light attack
* Heavy attack
* Combo chains
* Dodging
* Perfect dodge
* Blocking
* Perfect block
* Counter
* Parry
* Guard break
* Launch attacks
* Air combos
* Ground attacks
* Throws
* Grabs
* Finishers
* Special abilities
* Ultimates

Make the controls accessible but allow high skill expression.

---

# 17. CHARACTER SWITCHING

Create a party system.

Allow the player to control a team.

During major combat:

* Switch characters instantly
* Chain abilities
* Perform assists
* Create combo attacks
* Combine powers
* Trigger team attacks

Every character should feel different.

Do NOT make characters simple stat swaps.

# 97. DYNAMIC EVENTS BASED ON PLAYER

* 500 identical collectibles

* Copy-pasted buildings
* Empty roads

* Unique events
* Interesting locations
* Secrets
* Characters

NPCs look upward.

Lights flicker.

A strange anomaly appears.

Music changes.

A massive enemy falls onto the road.

Combat begins.

The player can either fight, escape or investigate.

Moments like this should happen organically.

The clothing should match the **premium futuristic anime aesthetic** of the game, with the kind of layered, elegant, fashion-forward designs seen in modern anime games such as the general clothing feel of **Baizhi** and **Aether** from Wuthering Waves, while remaining completely **original** and not copying their exact outfits, designs, logos, patterns, accessories, or copyrighted assets.
## CLOTHING STYLE
Create clothing that feels:
* High-quality anime
* Futuristic
* Elegant
* Stylish
* Detailed
* Layered
* Premium
* Slightly sci-fi
* Suitable for a large open-world anime RPG
* Visually interesting from both close and gameplay camera distances
Avoid generic basic clothing.
Do NOT make the wardrobe consist mainly of simple T-shirts, plain jeans, basic hoodies, or low-detail clothing.
Use sophisticated combinations such as:
* Long layered coats
* Futuristic jackets
* Oversized elegant outerwear
* High-collar coats
* Asymmetrical jackets
* Long flowing coats
* Short futuristic jackets
* Layered shirts
* Tunics
* Techwear-inspired clothing
* Elegant futuristic uniforms
* Academy/school outfits
* Casual city outfits
* Adventure outfits
* Combat-inspired outfits
* Formal outfits
* Summer outfits
* Winter outfits
* Space-station outfits
* Sci-fi exploration outfits
## LAYERING
The clothing system should support multiple layers that visually work together.
For example:
Base layer → shirt/top → vest → jacket/coat → accessories.
Clothing should have proper:
* Sleeves
* Collars
* Cuffs
* Seams
* Folds
* Belts
* Straps
* Buttons
* Zippers
* Fabric thickness
* Layer separation
* Natural cloth silhouettes
Do not make clothing appear as flat textures painted onto the character.
## MATERIALS
Use high-quality PBR materials.
Support materials such as:
* Fabric
* Cotton
* Leather
* Synthetic fabric
* Rubber
* Metal
* Carbon-fibre-like materials
* Transparent/translucent materials where appropriate
* Futuristic technical fabrics
Clothing should respond properly to:
* Lumen lighting
* Shadows
* Reflections
* Night lighting
* Neon lighting
* Interior lighting
* Daylight
## ORIGINAL ANIME DESIGNS
Create original clothing silhouettes inspired by futuristic anime fashion rather than copying existing characters.
Use:
* Asymmetry
* Layered silhouettes
* Long coats
* Flowing fabric
* Technical panels
* Decorative straps
* Subtle glowing elements
* Metallic details
* Elegant trims
* Futuristic fasteners
* Small holographic/technology details
Keep the designs believable and wearable.
## CHARACTER CREATOR INTEGRATION
Integrate clothing into the existing character creator.
Users should be able to change:
* Tops
* Jackets
* Coats
* Bottoms
* Shoes
* Gloves
* Accessories
* Outer layers
Changing clothing should immediately update the visible player character.
Do not replace the character model when changing clothes.
## CLOTHING COLOURS
Provide multiple colour variations for clothing.
Allow combinations such as:
* Black
* White
* Grey
* Navy
* Deep blue
* Silver
* Red
* Purple
* Cyan
* Gold
* Other tasteful futuristic colour combinations
Avoid making every outfit neon.
Use neon/glowing elements as accents rather than covering entire outfits in glowing materials.
## OUTFIT PRESETS
Create complete outfit presets including:
### Academy
Futuristic anime school uniform suitable for the Aetherveil academy.
### City Casual
Modern futuristic everyday clothing.
### Explorer
Layered clothing designed for exploration of cities, ruins, planets and other environments.
### Combat
Practical futuristic combat-inspired clothing while remaining stylish and anime-inspired.
### Formal
Elegant futuristic formalwear.
### Winter
Layered coats and warm clothing suitable for cold environments.
### Space
Futuristic clothing suitable for orbital stations and space environments.
## ANIMATION COMPATIBILITY
Clothing must work correctly with the existing character animations.
Avoid:
* Severe clipping
* Floating clothing
* Broken sleeves
* Clothing intersecting the body
* Accessories permanently stuck in incorrect positions
Where possible, use proper skeletal clothing/mesh techniques and cloth simulation only where useful and performant.
## PERFORMANCE
Do not create hundreds of separate expensive clothing systems.
Use efficient:
* Materials
* Meshes
* LODs
* Texture resolution
* Asset reuse
* Instancing where appropriate
The clothing system must remain suitable for an open-world game with multiple NPCs.
## NPC CLOTHING
NPCs should also use the clothing system.
Give different NPC groups appropriate outfits:
* Students
* Teachers
* Scientists
* Shop workers
* Civilians
* Security
* Explorers
* Researchers
* Faction members
NPC clothing should help visually distinguish their roles.

If high-quality custom clothing assets cannot be generated immediately, build the **proper clothing-system architecture first** and clearly identify any asset that still requires a final-quality custom model.
Do not claim that clothing is finished if it is only a placeholder.
The final goal is a **premium original anime-futuristic wardrobe system** that makes the player character look like they belong in a high-budget anime open-world RPG.

The protagonists encounter the primary antagonist.

They fight.

This is a REAL gameplay encounter.

The antagonist defeats them.

After the defeat:

- their equipment is lost
- their previous equipment is removed
- their wardrobe state changes
- story flags update
- the player starts the main adventure with reduced equipment
- the mystery is established

The encounter should transition naturally into the first playable exploration section.

# AETHERVEIL

## FULL 3D OPEN-WORLD ANIME LIFE-SIM RPG

Build a REAL playable 3D game called **Aetherveil**.

This is NOT a webpage containing links to existing games.

This is NOT a game menu pretending to be a 3D game.

This is NOT a low-poly prototype.

I want an actual playable third-person 3D anime open-world experience with a real controllable character, explorable world, NPCs, buildings, interiors, quests, story, character customisation, interactions and progression.

The visual target should be a polished modern anime 3D game inspired by the overall quality and presentation of games such as **Wuthering Waves** and other high-quality anime RPGs, while using ORIGINAL characters, locations, models, names and assets.

Wuthering Waves is ONLY a visual and gameplay-quality reference.

Do NOT copy copyrighted characters or assets from existing games.

# 1. CORE GAME

Create a large explorable anime-inspired open world.

The player controls their own fully customisable anime character.

The game should be third-person.

LOCK THESE DESIGN DECISIONS FOR THE ENTIRE GAME. DO NOT ASK ME THESE QUESTIONS AGAIN.

## CORE GAMEPLAY LOOP

Combine ALL THREE gameplay loops:

1. EXPLORE → DISCOVER → TAKE QUESTS → COMPLETE QUESTS
2. INTERACT WITH NPCS → BUILD FRIENDSHIPS/RELATIONSHIPS → EXPERIENCE EVENTS AND STORIES
3. EXPLORE/COMBAT → COLLECT RESOURCES → CRAFT/UPGRADE → BECOME STRONGER

The player should be free to switch between these activities at any time.

There must NOT be one single forced gameplay loop.

The game should feel like a living anime world where the player chooses what they want to do each day.

Bosses should have:

* Distinct designs
* Unique abilities
* Multiple phases
* Unique arenas
* Story significance
* Personality or identity where appropriate
* Dialogue
* Environmental effects
* Cinematic introductions
* Cinematic conclusions

Some bosses should be mysterious rather than immediately explained.

---

# ⚡ CHARACTER COMBOS

Characters who have strong relationships should sometimes have special cooperative interactions.

Examples:

Two rivals temporarily cooperate.

Two close friends coordinate an attack.

Two characters protect each other.

A character saves another during a boss battle.

A relationship milestone unlocks a unique cooperative sequence.

These should be earned through the story.

---

# 🧠 CHOICES + CONSEQUENCES

Where practical, allow players to make choices.

Choices can influence:

* Relationships
* Dialogue
* Character reactions
* Mission outcomes
* Optional scenes
* Faction relationships
* Character trust
* Future conversations

Do not create fake choices where every option produces exactly the same result.

Not every choice needs to radically change the entire game.

Small consequences can make the world feel responsive.

---

# 🏫 DAILY LIFE

Between major adventures, allow the player to experience normal life.

Examples:

* Attend school/university
* Visit cafes
* Go shopping
* Explore the city
* Meet friends
* Train
* Visit character homes
* Attend festivals
* Go to beaches
* Explore parks
* Participate in activities
* Discover side stories
* Talk with NPCs

This creates contrast between peaceful life and the major cosmic storyline.

---

# 🗺️ SIDE STORIES

Create hundreds of potential smaller stories over the lifetime of the game.

Examples:

A character needs help with a personal problem.

Two friends have fallen out.

A mysterious NPC keeps appearing in different locations.

A cafe owner has a strange secret.

A student is investigating something unusual.

A character wants to prove themselves.

A forgotten location contains evidence about the world's history.

A funny side mission unexpectedly becomes important later.

Side stories should sometimes connect back to the main storyline.

---

# 👑 FACTIONS

Create original factions with conflicting goals.

Each faction should have:

* Leaders
* Members
* Philosophy
* Goals
* Resources
* Locations
* Allies
* Enemies
* Secrets

Do not make every faction purely good or evil.

Give them understandable motivations.

---

# 🌠 THE CENTRAL MYSTERY

Create a major mystery that keeps the player asking:

**"WHAT IS REALLY HAPPENING TO THIS WORLD?"**

Reveal information gradually.

Use:

* Strange locations
* Hidden recordings
* Character memories
* Ancient technology
* NPC rumours
* Environmental storytelling
* Strange events
* Secret missions
* Character dialogue
* Discoverable documents
* Major cinematic revelations

Do not explain everything immediately.

---

# 🎥 CINEMATIC DIRECTOR

Major story moments should use a cinematic presentation system.

Where appropriate use:

* Dynamic cameras
* Camera cuts
* Close-ups
* Wide environmental shots
* Character focus
* Facial expressions
* Body language
* Lighting changes
* VFX
* Niagara
* Music
* Sound effects
* Environmental reactions

The goal is for major scenes to feel like actual anime episodes or AAA game cinematics.

---

# 🌅 PEACE → CHAOS → EMOTION

Use strong pacing.

A chapter could begin with:

Funny school scene

↓

Friends hanging out

↓

Exploration

↓

Small mystery

↓

Character interaction

↓

Strange discovery

↓

Danger

↓

Battle

↓

Major revelation

↓

Emotional aftermath

↓

Quiet character scene

↓

Next adventure

This contrast should be one of Aetherveil's defining qualities.

---

# 🧩 CHARACTER MEMORY

Characters should remember important events where technically practical.

For example:

If the player helped a character during an important mission, later dialogue can reference it.

If two characters had an argument, they should not immediately behave as if it never happened.

If the player makes an important relationship choice, future interactions can acknowledge it.

Avoid giving characters unlimited memory.

Prioritize important story events and relationship milestones.

---

# 🎭 CHARACTER ARCS

Every major character should have an arc.

A character can:

* Change their beliefs
* Become more confident
* Overcome fear
* Repair a friendship
* Become a rival
* Discover their past
* Lose something important
* Gain something important
* Learn to trust others
* Become a leader
* Make mistakes
* Redeem themselves

Characters should feel different near the end of their arc than at the beginning.

---

# 🌌 MASSIVE ESCALATION

Eventually expand the story beyond the original city.

Introduce:

* Space travel
* Orbital stations
* Floating cities
* Alien environments
* Cosmic anomalies
* Ancient ruins
* Unknown dimensions
* Secret realms
* Massive research facilities
* Other civilizations
* Reality-changing events

The player should gradually realize:

**The city was only the beginning.**

---

Aetherveil should aim to deliver:

**Massive world**

The goal is not simply to make a game with a large map.

The goal is to create a world where players become attached to the characters and genuinely care about what happens to them.

# AETHERVEIL — ADVANCED ANIME FUTURISTIC CLOTHING SYSTEM

Add a full high-quality clothing and outfit system to Aetherveil.

The clothing should match the **premium futuristic anime aesthetic** of the game, with the kind of layered, elegant, fashion-forward designs seen in modern anime games such as the general clothing feel of **Baizhi** and **Aether** from Wuthering Waves, while remaining completely **original** and not copying their exact outfits, designs, logos, patterns, accessories, or copyrighted assets.

## CLOTHING STYLE

Create clothing that feels:

* High-quality anime
* Futuristic
* Elegant
* Stylish
* Detailed
* Layered
* Premium
* Slightly sci-fi
* Suitable for a large open-world anime RPG
* Visually interesting from both close and gameplay camera distances

Avoid generic basic clothing.

Do NOT make the wardrobe consist mainly of simple T-shirts, plain jeans, basic hoodies, or low-detail clothing.

Use sophisticated combinations such as:

* Long layered coats
* Futuristic jackets
* Oversized elegant outerwear
* High-collar coats
* Asymmetrical jackets
* Long flowing coats
* Short futuristic jackets
* Layered shirts
* Tunics
* Techwear-inspired clothing
* Elegant futuristic uniforms
* Academy/school outfits
* Casual city outfits
* Adventure outfits
* Combat-inspired outfits
* Formal outfits
* Summer outfits
* Winter outfits
* Space-station outfits
* Sci-fi exploration outfits

## LAYERING

The clothing system should support multiple layers that visually work together.

For example:

Base layer → shirt/top → vest → jacket/coat → accessories.

Clothing should have proper:

* Sleeves
* Collars
* Cuffs
* Seams
* Folds
* Belts
* Straps
* Buttons
* Zippers
* Fabric thickness
* Layer separation
* Natural cloth silhouettes

Do not make clothing appear as flat textures painted onto the character.

## MATERIALS

Use high-quality PBR materials.

Support materials such as:

* Fabric
* Cotton
* Leather
* Synthetic fabric
* Rubber
* Metal
* Carbon-fibre-like materials
* Transparent/translucent materials where appropriate
* Futuristic technical fabrics

Clothing should respond properly to:

* Lumen lighting
* Shadows
* Reflections
* Night lighting
* Neon lighting
* Interior lighting
* Daylight

## ORIGINAL ANIME DESIGNS

Create original clothing silhouettes inspired by futuristic anime fashion rather than copying existing characters.

Use:

* Asymmetry
* Layered silhouettes
* Long coats
* Flowing fabric
* Technical panels
* Decorative straps
* Subtle glowing elements
* Metallic details
* Elegant trims
* Futuristic fasteners
* Small holographic/technology details

Keep the designs believable and wearable.

## CHARACTER CREATOR INTEGRATION

Integrate clothing into the existing character creator.

Users should be able to change:

* Tops
* Jackets
* Coats
* Bottoms
* Shoes
* Gloves
* Accessories
* Outer layers

Changing clothing should immediately update the visible player character.

Do not replace the character model when changing clothes.

## CLOTHING COLOURS

Provide multiple colour variations for clothing.

Allow combinations such as:

* Black
* White
* Grey
* Navy
* Deep blue
* Silver
* Red
* Purple
* Cyan
* Gold
* Other tasteful futuristic colour combinations

Avoid making every outfit neon.

Use neon/glowing elements as accents rather than covering entire outfits in glowing materials.

## OUTFIT PRESETS

Create complete outfit presets including:

### Academy

Futuristic anime school uniform suitable for the Aetherveil academy.

### City Casual

Modern futuristic everyday clothing.

### Explorer

Layered clothing designed for exploration of cities, ruins, planets and other environments.

### Combat

Practical futuristic combat-inspired clothing while remaining stylish and anime-inspired.

### Formal

Elegant futuristic formalwear.

### Winter

Layered coats and warm clothing suitable for cold environments.

### Space

Futuristic clothing suitable for orbital stations and space environments.

## ANIMATION COMPATIBILITY

Clothing must work correctly with the existing character animations.

Avoid:

* Severe clipping
* Floating clothing
* Broken sleeves
* Clothing intersecting the body
* Accessories permanently stuck in incorrect positions

Where possible, use proper skeletal clothing/mesh techniques and cloth simulation only where useful and performant.

## PERFORMANCE

Do not create hundreds of separate expensive clothing systems.

Use efficient:

* Materials
* Meshes
* LODs
* Texture resolution
* Asset reuse
* Instancing where appropriate

The clothing system must remain suitable for an open-world game with multiple NPCs.

## NPC CLOTHING

NPCs should also use the clothing system.

Give different NPC groups appropriate outfits:

* Students
* Teachers
* Scientists
* Shop workers
* Civilians
* Security
* Explorers
* Researchers
* Faction members

NPC clothing should help visually distinguish their roles.

## IMPORTANT

Do not use placeholder cubes, primitive meshes, stick figures, or obviously unfinished placeholder clothing as the final implementation.

If high-quality custom clothing assets cannot be generated immediately, build the **proper clothing-system architecture first** and clearly identify any asset that still requires a final-quality custom model.

Do not claim that clothing is finished if it is only a placeholder.

The final goal is a **premium original anime-futuristic wardrobe system** that makes the player character look like they belong in a high-budget anime open-world RPG.

NPC INTELLIGENCE:

* NPCs should have individual personalities, names, interests, jobs, routines, relationships and opinions.
* Give NPCs memory of important interactions with the player.
* NPCs should react differently depending on personality, mood, relationship level and previous conversations.
* NPCs should have believable daily schedules: waking up, working, eating, shopping, socialising, travelling home and sleeping.
* NPCs should be able to react to events happening around them.
* Avoid repetitive generic dialogue.

FREE-FORM NPC CHAT:

The player should be able to type things like:

* skin tone
* hairstyle
* age

Major characters should be immediately recognizable.

---

# 35. CHARACTER AGE

Major playable characters should be clearly adult.

Adult characters can have sophisticated stylish designs.

School-age characters must remain age-appropriate.

---

# 36. CHARACTER SILHOUETTES

Each playable character must be recognizable as a silhouette.

If all characters were shown in black silhouette, players should still be able to tell them apart.

---

# 37. CHARACTER COLOUR LANGUAGE

Do not give every character random rainbow colours.

Each character gets a controlled palette.

Use combinations such as:

* black + silver + blue
* white + graphite + cyan
* charcoal + violet
* cream + gold
* dark green + silver
* navy + white
* burgundy + black
* grey + turquoise

But create individual palettes.

---

# 38. WEAPONS

Each playable character should have a visually appropriate weapon.

Weapons should:

* match the character
* have detailed geometry
* use PBR materials
* have unique silhouettes
* have subtle technology
* integrate with animations

---

# 39. VFX IDENTITY

Every playable character should have unique visual effects.

Effects should communicate:

* element/ability
* character personality
* combat role

Avoid copying another game's exact VFX.

---

# 40. ANIMATION IDENTITY

Characters should not all move identically.

Give them different:

* idle poses
* walking styles
* attack rhythms
* dodge animations
* combat stances
* victory animations

Personality should appear through animation.

---

# 41. NPC AI

All important NPCs should connect to Nova's AI system.

They should have:

* schedules
* navigation
* dialogue
* relationships
* memory
* jobs
* locations
* routines

---

# 42. NPC CLOTHING VARIATION

Create multiple clothing variations.

Avoid:

NPC 1 = same body + different colour.

Instead vary:

* jackets
* shirts
* trousers
* skirts where appropriate
* coats
* shoes
* accessories
* bags
* uniforms
* work clothing

---

# 45. FINAL QUALITY STANDARD

The cast must look like it belongs in the same premium game.

The goal is:

**ORIGINAL NOVA CHARACTERS**

with the sophistication, detail and fashion-conscious design language of premium modern action RPGs.

NOT:

* generic AI characters
* low-poly characters
* random clothing
* identical faces
* anime drawings
* flat illustrations
* placeholder mannequins

Every major character should look intentionally designed.

They must be usable in Unreal Engine.

# 48. FINAL CAST GOAL

Nova should eventually have a cast where players can say:

"I recognize that character immediately."

because every character has:

* unique silhouette
* unique face
* unique outfit
* unique personality
* unique combat identity
* unique story
* unique animations
* unique visual effects

Build the roster as a cohesive universe rather than a collection of random characters.

# NOVA — COMPLETE ORIGINAL CHARACTER CAST
# NOVA — MASSIVE STORY-DRIVEN CAST + PERSONALITY-BASED CHARACTER DESIGN

Expand the Nova cast substantially.

Do not create random characters simply to increase the number.

Every important character must exist for a reason within the story, world, factions, quests, locations or gameplay.

The cast should feel like a real population of a massive futuristic world.

# 1. STORY-FIRST CHARACTER DESIGN

Every major character must have a PURPOSE.

For every character determine:

* name
* age category
* personality
* occupation
* faction
* home/location
* relationships
* story purpose
* quests
* motivations
* fears
* goals
* secrets
* abilities
* combat role if playable
* clothing style
* hairstyle
* accessories
* weapon/equipment
* visual effects
* daily schedule

Do not create a character before determining why they belong in Nova.

---

# 2. STORY CONNECTION

Characters must connect to the existing Nova storyline.

Create characters associated with:

## THE PROTAGONISTS

Friends, rivals, mentors, allies, enemies and mysterious figures connected to the protagonists.

## THE CITY

People who actually make the city function.

## THE SCHOOL

Students, teachers, staff, researchers and important story figures.

## THE CAFE

Owner, workers, regular customers, suppliers and recurring characters.

## RESEARCH ORGANIZATIONS

Scientists, directors, engineers, technicians and security.

## CITY SECURITY

Officers, commanders, investigators and specialists.

## ORBITAL SOCIETY

Pilots, engineers, researchers, station workers and explorers.

## UNDERGROUND NETWORK

Hackers, smugglers, informants, fixers and mysterious contacts.

## EXPLORER GROUPS

Scouts, researchers, adventurers and guides.

## COSMIC ANOMALY STORY

Researchers, witnesses, survivors, investigators and people affected by anomalies.

---

# 3. CHARACTER RELATIONSHIP WEB

Do not make characters exist independently.

Build relationships between them.

Examples:

Character A knows Character B.

Character B dislikes Character C.

Character C works for Faction X.

Character D secretly knows information about Character A.

Character E is connected to the protagonist's past.

Character F is a rival.

Character G is a mentor.

Character H becomes an ally after a quest.

Character I betrays the group.

Character J has information needed to unlock a hidden location.

Relationships should influence:

* dialogue
* quests
* schedules
* story flags
* missions
* character unlocks
* combat
* future conversations

---

# 4. PERSONALITY-FIRST DESIGN

THIS IS EXTREMELY IMPORTANT.

Do NOT design the clothing first.

First determine the character's personality.

Then design the character around that personality.

A:

calm scientist

should NOT dress like

a reckless street fighter.

A:

formal executive

should NOT dress like

a mechanic.

A:

rebellious hacker

should NOT dress like

a security officer.

A:

quiet explorer

should NOT dress like

a celebrity.

Clothing must communicate personality.

---

# 5. PERSONALITY → CLOTHING SYSTEM

For every character ask:

WHAT WOULD THIS PERSON ACTUALLY CHOOSE TO WEAR?

Consider:

* personality
* occupation
* social status
* faction
* hobbies
* environment
* combat role
* age
* lifestyle
* cultural influences
* practicality

Then design the outfit.

# MASTER PRIORITY ORDER
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use this priority order whenever several tasks compete:

PRIORITY 0 — SAFETY AND PROJECT PRESERVATION
- Never destroy the existing project.
- Never wipe Content, Config, Source, Saved, Plugins, or working systems.
- Never overwrite important assets without inspection.
- Never disable streaming merely to make a feature easier.
- Never silently change locked design decisions.
- Never introduce destructive migration without backups or a reversible path.

PRIORITY 1 — PLAYABILITY
- The player must always have a usable control loop.
- Core movement, camera, interaction, combat, dialogue, quests, inventory and saving must remain functional.
- A broken core loop takes priority over cosmetic polish.

PRIORITY 2 — WORLD AND CHARACTER QUALITY
- Build meaningful environments.
- Build believable NPCs.
- Build distinctive characters.
- Build authored story content.
- Avoid generic placeholder content.

PRIORITY 3 — SYSTEMIC DEPTH
- Add interconnected systems only after their dependencies are stable.
- Prefer reusable data-driven systems.

PRIORITY 4 — PRESENTATION
- UI, animation, VFX, lighting, audio, cinematics and environmental polish.

PRIORITY 5 — OPTIONAL DEPTH
- Minigames, collections, advanced housing, photo mode, advanced accessibility, extra activities and other secondary systems.

Never sacrifice a stable foundational system just to add a flashy secondary feature.

# PLAYER EXPERIENCE — THE COMPLETE MOMENT-TO-MOMENT LOOP
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Aetherveil should support many valid play styles without forcing one repetitive loop.

A player may:
- Explore.
- Attend school.
- Work or help at businesses.
- Socialise.
- Build friendships.
- Pursue romance where age-appropriate and narratively appropriate.
- Investigate mysteries.
- Join or oppose factions.
- Fight enemies.
- Collect materials.
- Craft.
- Cook.
- Decorate housing.
- Drive or travel.
- Take photographs.
- Discover secrets.
- Complete character stories.
- Follow the main story.
- Ignore the main story for long periods.
- Return to old locations after new abilities unlock.
- Change clothing.
- Change playable characters.
- Train characters.
- Hunt for rare resources.
- Solve environmental puzzles.
- Participate in festivals and timed events.
- Explore cosmic locations.
- Discover optional lore.
- Replay important memories/cinematics.

The game must recognise these activities and feed them back into:
- reputation,
- relationships,
- knowledge,
- quest availability,
- world state,
- character development,
- economy,
- faction state,
- collection completion,
- story flags,
- exploration progress,
- player statistics,
- achievements.

Do not make the world pretend nothing happened after the player completes major events.
