# CHARACTER PROGRESSION — DEEP RPG ARCHITECTURE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a layered progression architecture.

PLAYER PROGRESSION
- Overall player/account progression where appropriate.
- Story progression.
- Exploration progression.
- Social progression.
- Knowledge/codex progression.
- Crafting progression.
- Combat mastery.
- School/life progression.
- Reputation.
- Achievement progression.

PLAYABLE CHARACTER PROGRESSION
Each playable character can have:
- Level.
- Base attributes.
- Combat role.
- Weapon proficiency.
- Ability levels.
- Passive traits.
- Active abilities.
- Ultimate/special ability.
- Movement modifiers where appropriate.
- Character-specific progression nodes.
- Relationship/story unlocks.
- Equipment slots.
- Cosmetic slots.
- Outfit sets.
- Character memories.
- Character-specific quests.

Do not make progression a simple number that only increases damage.
Every major progression milestone should unlock something meaningful:
- a mechanic,
- an ability,
- a combo,
- a traversal option,
- a social option,
- a crafting recipe,
- a story branch,
- a new interaction,
- a cosmetic,
- a passive,
- a quality-of-life improvement,
- or access to a new location.

Avoid runaway stat inflation.
Keep numbers readable and balanceable.
Use data assets/data tables rather than hard-coded values where practical.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# SKILL TREES AND MASTERY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Implement a flexible skill/mastery framework.

Possible branches:
- Combat.
- Mobility.
- Exploration.
- Social.
- Crafting.
- Technology.
- Investigation.
- Survival.
- School/life skills.
- Character-specific mastery.

Skill nodes may provide:
- new actions,
- reduced stamina cost,
- improved dodge windows,
- improved parry windows,
- alternate combo routes,
- enhanced abilities,
- traversal interactions,
- dialogue knowledge checks,
- crafting efficiency,
- gathering efficiency,
- vehicle improvements,
- social opportunities,
- unique character interactions.

Requirements:
- Skill descriptions must explain real effects.
- Locked nodes must show meaningful requirements.
- Respec rules must be fair and clear.
- Skill changes must save correctly.
- UI must show current and future effects.
- No fake skill nodes.
- Every unlocked skill must be testable in gameplay.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# COMBAT — PREMIUM ACTION RPG FOUNDATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Build a responsive action combat system with readable feedback.

CORE:
- Light attacks.
- Heavy attacks.
- Charged attacks where appropriate.
- Dodge.
- Perfect dodge.
- Guard/block where appropriate.
- Parry/counter where appropriate.
- Jump.
- Air attacks.
- Aerial launchers where appropriate.
- Character-specific skills.
- Ultimate/special ability.
- Character switching.
- Targeting/soft lock.
- Camera collision handling.
- Hit reactions.
- Stagger.
- Knockback.
- Knockdown.
- Recovery.
- Invulnerability windows.
- Interrupt rules.
- Damage categories.
- Status effects.
- Enemy resistance.
- Weak points.
- Critical hits where appropriate.

COMBAT FEEL:
- Input buffering should be deliberate and configurable.
- Animation cancel windows must be intentional.
- Hits should have clear audio, VFX, camera and animation feedback.
- Avoid excessive camera shake.
- Attacks should not feel like floating mannequins.
- Feet should remain grounded when appropriate.
- Character-specific movement should reinforce personality.

CHARACTER IDENTITY:
Every playable character should have a reason to exist mechanically.
Examples:
- Duelist: precision, parry, counterattacks.
- Engineer: deployables and battlefield control.
- Medic: healing/support.
- Archer: ranged weak-point pressure.
- Heavy: armor, stagger and area control.
- Hacker: technology disruption and enemy manipulation.
- Aerial specialist: mobility and air combos.
These are examples only; use the existing Aetherveil cast and Master Prompt as the source of truth for final identities.

Do not copy combat kits from existing games.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# COMBAT — ENEMY AI
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Enemies must understand combat states rather than simply walking toward the player.

Implement:
- Detection.
- Awareness.
- Suspicion.
- Search.
- Combat engagement.
- Retreat.
- Regroup.
- Flanking.
- Ranged positioning.
- Melee spacing.
- Ability selection.
- Ally support.
- Crowd-control reactions.
- Stagger reactions.
- Target switching.
- Threat evaluation.
- Environmental awareness.
- Navigation recovery.
- Death behaviour.
- Despawn rules.
- Encounter reset rules.

Different enemy archetypes:
- Melee rushers.
- Defensive units.
- Ranged attackers.
- Supports.
- Controllers.
- Assassins.
- Tanks.
- Scouts.
- Summoners.
- Flying enemies.
- Swarm enemies.
- Elite enemies.
- Mini-bosses.
- Bosses.

Enemies should communicate internally through readable behaviours.
Bosses need:
- phases,
- telegraphs,
- punish windows,
- transitions,
- environmental interaction where appropriate,
- escalation,
- unique mechanics,
- recovery rules,
- rewards,
- narrative context.

Never make difficulty simply mean multiplying enemy health by a huge number.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# COMBAT — DAMAGE, STATUS AND BUILDCRAFT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a data-driven combat calculation layer.

Support where appropriate:
- Physical damage.
- Energy damage.
- Elemental/affinity damage if compatible with Aetherveil lore.
- Armor.
- Resistance.
- Vulnerability.
- Stagger damage.
- Healing.
- Shields.
- Damage-over-time.
- Buffs.
- Debuffs.
- Crowd control.
- Cleansing.
- Interrupts.

All calculations should be deterministic and inspectable.
Do not hide balancing values inside random Blueprint graphs when a data asset/table is more appropriate.

Buildcraft should allow different viable configurations rather than one mandatory build.
Equipment can modify:
- attack style,
- cooldowns,
- stamina,
- defense,
- elemental effects,
- critical behaviour,
- support strength,
- exploration utility.

Avoid loot systems that require gambling or paid randomisation.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# TRAVERSAL — MAKE THE WORLD FUN TO MOVE THROUGH
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Movement itself must be enjoyable.

Implement and polish:
- Walk.
- Jog.
- Sprint.
- Jump.
- Fall.
- Landing.
- Climb where appropriate.
- Vault.
- Mantle.
- Ledge interaction.
- Crouch where appropriate.
- Swimming.
- Water entry/exit.
- Slopes.
- Stairs.
- Ramps.
- Ladders where appropriate.
- Zip/rail traversal where the world supports it.
- Vehicles.
- Fast travel.
- Travel transitions.
- Character-specific traversal abilities.

Movement should respect:
- collision,
- animation,
- camera,
- stamina if used,
- world geometry,
- performance,
- streaming boundaries.

Do not add traversal mechanics that make the city harder to navigate.
Every traversal mechanic should improve exploration or combat.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# WORLD INTERACTION SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a universal interaction framework.

Interactions may include:
- Talk.
- Inspect.
- Pick up.
- Collect.
- Open.
- Close.
- Sit.
- Sleep.
- Eat.
- Drink.
- Read.
- Use.
- Equip.
- Craft.
- Cook.
- Repair.
- Enter vehicle.
- Exit vehicle.
- Ride.
- Photograph.
- Investigate.
- Search.
- Push/pull where appropriate.
- Activate.
- Hack.
- Scan.
- Trade.
- Gift.
- Play.
- Practice.
- Train.

The interaction prompt must be context-sensitive.
Do not spam interaction markers everywhere.
Use distance, line of sight and object state to determine availability.

Every interactive object must handle:
- unavailable state,
- interaction state,
- success,
- failure,
- interruption,
- save/load state where needed.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# INVENTORY — COMPLETE ITEM ARCHITECTURE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Expand inventory into a robust item system.

Item categories:
- Weapons.
- Armor/equipment.
- Clothing.
- Accessories.
- Consumables.
- Food.
- Ingredients.
- Crafting materials.
- Quest items.
- Key items.
- Collectibles.
- Books/documents.
- Gifts.
- Furniture.
- Vehicle items.
- Cosmetic items.
- Upgrade materials.

Each item can support:
- unique ID,
- display name,
- description,
- icon,
- category,
- rarity where appropriate,
- stack size,
- weight if used,
- value,
- tags,
- usage rules,
- source,
- sellability,
- quest relevance,
- crafting relevance,
- persistence.

UI:
- search,
- filters,
- sorting,
- favourites,
- compare,
- stack splitting,
- quick use,
- item details,
- controller navigation,
- keyboard navigation.

Never lose items because of an accidental UI transition.
Autosave important inventory mutations.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# CRAFTING — DEEP BUT REASONABLE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create interconnected crafting.

Crafting families:
- Weapons.
- Weapon upgrades.
- Character equipment.
- Clothing modifications where appropriate.
- Consumables.
- Cooking.
- Medical items.
- Exploration equipment.
- Housing furniture.
- Decorations.
- Vehicle improvements.
- Quest-specific objects.

Crafting stations can be location-specific:
- Workshop.
- Laboratory.
- Kitchen.
- Engineering bench.
- Medical station.
- Research station.
- Field kit.

Recipes should be discoverable through:
- story,
- NPCs,
- shops,
- exploration,
- research,
- achievements,
- experimentation.

Use meaningful recipe requirements.
Do not force repetitive grinding.
Allow players to understand exactly what they need.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# ECONOMY — A LIVING, FAIR ECONOMY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a believable economy.

Support:
- Currency.
- Purchases.
- Sales.
- Shop inventories.
- Shop schedules.
- Limited availability.
- Faction discounts.
- Relationship discounts.
- Quest rewards.
- Wages/rewards where appropriate.
- Crafting costs.
- Housing costs if the existing design supports them.
- Vehicle costs if applicable.

Shopkeepers should not behave like static vending machines.
Their stock can react to:
- time,
- location,
- events,
- story progression,
- supply,
- faction control,
- world incidents.

Avoid predatory systems.
No paid loot boxes.
No gambling.
No manipulative real-money mechanics hidden in gameplay.
If monetisation is ever added, it must be separate from core progression and must not compromise the single-player RPG design.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# NPC LIFE SIMULATION — SECOND LAYER
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Every important NPC should have a coherent life model.

NPC data can include:
- identity,
- home,
- work,
- school,
- faction,
- relationships,
- schedule,
- personality,
- interests,
- dislikes,
- fears,
- goals,
- knowledge,
- memories,
- current activity,
- current mood,
- current location,
- health/safety state where relevant,
- dialogue availability.

Daily schedule examples:
- Wake.
- Prepare.
- Commute.
- Work/class.
- Lunch.
- Social activity.
- Errands.
- Leisure.
- Return home.
- Sleep.

Schedules must bend around:
- rain,
- festivals,
- emergencies,
- combat,
- story events,
- holidays,
- faction incidents,
- player actions.

Do not teleport important NPCs without a narrative/system reason.
When schedules must use simulated movement for performance, preserve believable continuity.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# NPC SOCIAL GRAPH
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Build a relationship graph between NPCs.

Relationships can contain:
- friendship,
- rivalry,
- trust,
- family,
- mentorship,
- employment,
- faction loyalty,
- romance where appropriate,
- resentment,
- debt,
- admiration,
- fear.

NPC relationships can influence:
- dialogue,
- schedules,
- group gatherings,
- rumours,
- quests,
- shop availability,
- faction reactions,
- story branches.

The player should sometimes learn about the world indirectly through NPC relationships.
Do not make every NPC's relationships revolve around the player.
The city must feel like people have lives independent of the protagonist.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# NPC MEMORY AND REACTIVE DIALOGUE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Expand the dynamic dialogue architecture.

GAME STATE → SITUATION MANAGER → LOCAL QWEN → STRUCTURED DIALOGUE → VALIDATION → KOKORO → AUDIO CACHE → NPC PERFORMANCE

Dialogue context may include:
- player location,
- current quest,
- completed quests,
- recent events,
- NPC memories,
- relationship score,
- faction reputation,
- time,
- weather,
- player outfit,
- active character,
- recent combat,
- nearby NPCs,
- story chapter,
- player choices,
- discovered secrets,
- inventory items relevant to conversation,
- school status,
- world state.

The local model must NOT be allowed to invent irreversible lore freely.
Use a lore/context layer with approved facts.
Generated dialogue should be validated against:
- character personality,
- known lore,
- age appropriateness,
- current quest state,
- world state,
- relationship state.

Use deterministic fallbacks if generation fails.
Cache successful generated dialogue/audio where appropriate.
Never make gameplay depend on an external service being available during a critical story moment.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# QUEST SYSTEM — AAA-STYLE DATA MODEL
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Build quests as data-driven state machines.

Quest states:
- Locked.
- Available.
- Accepted.
- Active.
- Objective progress.
- Optional objective progress.
- Failed.
- Completed.
- Turn-in.
- Branch.
- Consequence.
- Archived.

Objective types:
- Travel.
- Talk.
- Investigate.
- Collect.
- Defeat.
- Protect.
- Escort.
- Follow.
- Photograph.
- Craft.
- Deliver.
- Attend.
- Wait.
- Choose.
- Solve puzzle.
- Interact.
- Survive.
- Discover.
- Stealth.
- Race.
- Social challenge.

Quest requirements can use:
- story flags,
- relationship levels,
- faction reputation,
- time,
- weather,
- location,
- character ownership,
- item ownership,
- knowledge,
- previous quests.

Every quest needs:
- clear objective communication,
- failure handling,
- recovery,
- save/load,
- journal entry,
- rewards,
- consequences,
- testing.

Avoid quests that are only "walk here and press button" unless used intentionally as a short pacing beat.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# QUEST CONSEQUENCE ENGINE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Important choices should be able to alter:
- NPC relationships.
- Faction reputation.
- Available quests.
- Shop access.
- Dialogue.
- World events.
- Character availability.
- Locations.
- Enemy presence.
- Rewards.
- Future choices.
- Ending variables.

Not every choice must create a massive branch.
Use layered consequences:
- immediate,
- medium-term,
- long-term,
- cosmetic,
- social,
- mechanical,
- narrative.

The player should be able to understand consequences through story rather than a giant "THIS WILL CHANGE EVERYTHING" warning every time.
Do not railroad the player into one ending.

- day,
- week,
- month,
- season,
- school term,
- holidays,
- festivals,
- character birthdays if used,
- recurring events.

Calendar events should be data-driven.
NPC schedules can use calendar conditions.
Some shops, decorations, outfits and events can change seasonally.
Story-critical dates must be deterministic.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# WORLD ECOLOGY AND WILDLIFE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Make nature feel systemic.

Wildlife can have:
- species,
- habitat,
- time activity,
- weather preference,
- flee behaviour,
- group behaviour,
- audio,
- animation,
- spawn rules,
- despawn rules.

Plants can have:
- species,
- location,
- growth state,
- harvest state,
- respawn timing,
- weather/season conditions.

Do not fill the world with random creatures everywhere.
Use ecological zones and density budgets.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# ENVIRONMENTAL STORYTELLING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Every major district should communicate history and current life through:
- architecture,
- signage,
- advertisements,
- graffiti,
- posters,
- furniture,
- damaged areas,
- repairs,
- NPC conversations,
- shops,
- abandoned objects,
- lighting,
- weathering,
- sound.

Major story events should leave visible traces where appropriate.
The player should be able to understand parts of the world without reading a giant exposition dump.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# DESTRUCTION AND REACTIVE ENVIRONMENT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Where technically and performance-wise appropriate, add controlled environmental reaction:
- breakable props,
- combat impact marks,
- temporary debris,
- doors opening,
- lights failing,
- alarms,
- damaged objects,
- repaired objects after world events.

Do not introduce unrestricted destruction that breaks navigation, quests or streaming.
Use authored destruction states.
Persist only changes that matter.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# INTERIORS AND BUILDING SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create reusable interior architecture.

Building categories:
- homes,
- apartments,
- shops,
- restaurants,
- schools,
- offices,
- laboratories,
- clinics,
- stations,
- warehouses,
- entertainment venues,
- faction facilities,
- secret facilities.

Interiors need:
- believable entrances,
- navigation,
- lighting,
- interaction points,
- NPC schedules,
- audio zones,
- streaming,
- save-safe state.

Avoid fake doors that look usable unless clearly decorative.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# STEALTH AND INVESTIGATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Where supported by the existing story:
- visibility,
- sound,
- suspicion,
- hiding,
- patrol routes,
- distraction,
- investigation,
- evidence,
- scanning,
- clues,
- witness conversations.

Investigation should reward observation rather than simply following a glowing trail.
Clues must have data IDs and quest relevance.
Players should have enough information to reason toward solutions.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# PUZZLE SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a reusable puzzle framework.

Puzzle types:
- logic,
- sequence,
- symbols,
- environment,
- electrical routing,
- hacking,
- investigation,
- spatial,
- timing,
- traversal.

Each puzzle needs:
- state,
- reset,
- solution,
- hints,
- accessibility alternative where appropriate,
- reward,
- save/load.

Do not create puzzles that can permanently soft-lock the player.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# REPUTATION AND PUBLIC PERCEPTION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Track reputation separately from faction reputation when useful.

Public perception can respond to:
- completed quests,
- heroic actions,
- failures,
- school performance,
- public events,
- faction affiliation,
- visible outfit/context,
- rumours.

Use thresholds carefully.
Do not make reputation simply a second XP bar.
It should change how some NPCs treat the player and what opportunities appear.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# RELATIONSHIPS — DEEPER SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Relationships should be more than a single number.

Track:
- trust,
- familiarity,
- affection,
- respect,
- shared memories,
- compatibility,
- boundaries,
- unresolved conflicts,
- important promises.

Relationships should support:
- conversations,
- hangouts,
- gifts,
- shared activities,
- character quests,
- group events,
- disagreements,
- reconciliation,
- supportive moments,
- story consequences.

Romance should only exist where appropriate to the established characters and narrative.
Do not reduce relationships to a gift-spamming optimisation game.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# COMPANION SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

When companions are active:
- follow navigation,
- combat participation,
- formation,
- reactions,
- contextual dialogue,
- relationship behaviour,
- support abilities,
- revive/downed rules if applicable,
- environmental comments,
- quest-specific behaviour.

Companions should avoid:
- blocking doors,
- standing on top of the player,
- walking into walls,
- triggering unintended interactions,
- ruining stealth without reason.

Companion AI must degrade gracefully if navigation fails.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# PARTY SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a party framework if compatible with the established Aetherveil design.

Support:
- active party,
- reserve party,
- formation,
- character switching,
- party bonuses where appropriate,
- party dialogue,
- combat synergy,
- party-specific story reactions.

Switching should be fast but controlled.
Do not allow character switching to bypass every intended encounter mechanic.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# CHARACTER SYNERGY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Characters can have complementary abilities without requiring rigid roles.

Examples:
- setup → burst,
- mark → precision attack,
- shield → counter,
- crowd control → area damage,
- heal → offensive conversion,
- aerial launch → aerial follow-up.

Synergy should emerge from actual kits.
Do not force artificial elemental reactions if they conflict with Aetherveil lore.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# EQUIPMENT AND BUILD MANAGEMENT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Support equipment:
- weapon,
- defensive equipment,
- accessories,
- utility items,
- cosmetic slots.

Features:
- equip,
- compare,
- lock,
- favourite,
- upgrade,
- dismantle/sell where appropriate,
- loadouts,
- quick swap.

Loadouts should remember:
- character,
- equipment,
- skills,
- cosmetics where appropriate.

Never accidentally destroy equipped or favourite items.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# WARDROBE — ADVANCED SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Build a real wardrobe.

Categories:
- hair,
- headwear,
- top,
- bottom,
- outerwear,
- shoes,
- accessories,
- gloves,
- special/cosmic gear,
- school uniform,
- combat outfit.

Support:
- colour variants,
- material variants,
- saved outfits,
- outfit presets,
- location/event rules,
- NPC outfit variation,
- clothing damage/dirty states only if visually appropriate.

Clothing must respect:
- body proportions,
- animation,
- collision,
- character personality,
- climate,
- story context.

Do not use one generic outfit on every NPC.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# CHARACTER CREATOR — FULL
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Player character customisation can include:
- face presets,
- skin tone,
- eyes,
- eyebrows,
- hair,
- hair colour,
- face details,
- height within safe animation bounds,
- body proportions within rig limits,
- voice style,
- clothing,
- accessories.

Use constrained parameters that preserve animation quality.
Do not allow arbitrary proportions that break the skeleton.
All customisation must save and restore reliably.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# CHARACTER PRESENTATION STANDARD
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Aetherveil characters must look like complete characters, not icons or mannequin placeholders.

For every important character:
- readable silhouette,
- coherent face,
- expressive eyes,
- detailed hair,
- layered clothing,
- believable materials,
- accessories,
- correct scale,
- animation-ready rig,
- personality-consistent design,
- colour language,
- unique posture,
- unique idle set,
- unique VFX identity where relevant.

If a model-generation tool is available, use the existing Aetherveil pipeline.
MYMESHY generates actual assets.
VIBE3D prepares/refines geometry and Unreal-side asset data.
UNREAL MCP integrates assets.
Do not invent fake completion if generation/import failed.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# BOSS DESIGN FRAMEWORK
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Every major boss should have:
- identity,
- narrative reason,
- arena,
- visual language,
- readable attacks,
- phase structure,
- music identity,
- VFX identity,
- dialogue/voice,
- weaknesses,
- counterplay,
- rewards,
- post-battle world response.

Boss arenas must support:
- camera,
- navigation,
- collision,
- streaming,
- reset,
- death/retry.

Do not create bosses whose only mechanic is a huge health bar.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# DUNGEON AND INSTANCE FRAMEWORK
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create reusable dungeon architecture for:
- research facilities,
- ruins,
- underground locations,
- cosmic structures,
- faction bases,
- anomaly zones.

Dungeons may include:
- combat,
- exploration,
- puzzles,
- environmental storytelling,
- shortcuts,
- checkpoints,
- secrets,
- optional bosses,
- treasure,
- story moments.

Ensure streaming and memory remain controlled.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# SECRET AND DISCOVERY SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Secrets should be discoverable through:
- visual anomalies,
- unusual NPC behaviour,
- environmental clues,
- hidden paths,
- puzzles,
- time-of-day conditions,
- weather,
- faction reputation,
- character abilities,
- investigation.

Do not mark every secret on the map.
Secrets should reward:
- lore,
- cosmetics,
- equipment,
- collectibles,
- character scenes,
- shortcuts,
- optional story.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# COLLECTIBLES — MEANINGFUL COLLECTION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Collection categories may include:
- photographs,
- lore fragments,
- research notes,
- plants,
- wildlife,
- recipes,
- character memories,
- artifacts,
- music records,
- clothing,
- furniture.

Collection UI should show:
- found,
- missing,
- hints where appropriate,
- location category,
- description.

Do not create thousands of meaningless identical collectibles just to inflate completion time.

# ACHIEVEMENT SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Achievements can reward:
- exploration,
- story,
- combat mastery,
- relationships,
- school activities,
- crafting,
- photography,
- secrets,
- character progression,
- boss victories,
- unusual actions.

Achievements must be:
- persistent,
- readable,
- non-destructive,
- tested.

Do not make achievements require abusive grinding.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# NEW GAME PLUS AND REPLAYABILITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

If compatible with the final narrative:
- New Game Plus.
- Story replay.
- Cinematic replay.
- Boss rematch.
- Character quest replay.
- Challenge modes.
- Completion tracking.

NG+ must clearly define what carries over.
Do not break story flags.
Do not duplicate quest rewards incorrectly.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# SAVE SYSTEM — ENTERPRISE-LEVEL ROBUSTNESS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The save system must protect player progress.

Use:
- manual save where appropriate,
- autosave,
- checkpoint saves,
- multiple save slots where practical,
- backup/recovery,
- versioning,
- migration,
- corruption detection,
- safe-write strategy,
- atomic save operations.

Never save half-written critical state.
If a save fails, notify the player and preserve the previous known-good save.
Test:
- save during quest,
- save after combat,
- save in housing,
- save after inventory mutation,
- save during relationship change,
- save after world event,
- save after character switch,
- save before/after travel.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# SETTINGS AND ACCESSIBILITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a serious settings menu.

Gameplay:
- difficulty,
- aim assistance where relevant,
- camera sensitivity,
- invert axes,
- vibration,
- subtitles,
- subtitle size,
- speaker names,
- text speed,
- skip controls,
- tutorial hints,
- HUD visibility.

Accessibility:
- colour-safe UI,
- scalable text,
- reduced motion,
- reduced camera shake,
- reduced flash intensity,
- audio sliders,
- mono audio where appropriate,
- controller remapping,
- keyboard remapping,
- hold/toggle options where safe,
- motion sensitivity options.

Graphics:
- resolution,
- window mode,
- frame cap,
- quality preset,
- textures,
- shadows,
- effects,
- foliage,
- view distance,
- post-processing,
- upscaling,
- anti-aliasing,
- reflections,
- VFX density.

All settings must actually apply and persist.

# MAIN MENU — PREMIUM FINAL PRESENTATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The main menu is a living part of Aetherveil.

Required:
- high-quality background scene,
- dynamic lighting,
- subtle environmental animation,
- original music,
- title treatment,
- New Game,
- Continue,
- Load Game,
- Settings,
- Extras,
- Credits,
- Exit where platform-appropriate.

Background can reflect:
- time,
- story progression,
- unlocked characters,
- major world states,
- seasonal conditions.

Buttons need:
- hover,
- focus,
- press,
- disabled states,
- controller navigation,
- keyboard navigation,
- sound,
- animation.

Never use a flat placeholder menu and call it final.

# LOADING SCREENS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Loading screens should be useful and polished.

Show:
- Aetherveil visual identity,
- subtle animation,
- gameplay tips,
- lore facts,
- controls,
- character information,
- location information,
- progress indicator where technically accurate.

Never display false loading percentages.
Do not freeze the UI if the engine is legitimately loading.
Use asynchronous loading and streaming wherever appropriate.

# HUD — INFORMATION WITHOUT CLUTTER
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a responsive HUD.

Possible elements:
- health,
- stamina,
- abilities,
- party,
- active objective,
- interaction prompt,
- minimap/compass,
- quest state,
- combat status,
- buffs/debuffs.

HUD should:
- scale,
- animate,
- hide when unnecessary,
- support controller focus,
- support accessibility,
- avoid blocking cinematic composition.

Do not show every piece of information simultaneously.

Maintain one visual language across:
- main menu,
- phone,
- inventory,
- map,
- character roster,
- wardrobe,
- housing,
- shops,
- dialogue,
- codex.

Apps can include:
- messages,

- camera,
- photos,
- music,
- quests,
- social feed,
- school schedule,
- weather,
- notes,
- codex,
- settings,
- emergency alerts.

Phone content should react to:
- story,
- relationships,
- world events,
- time,
- location.

Do not create a fake phone that only opens static screenshots.
Every app must have real gameplay purpose.

# MESSAGING AND SOCIAL FEED
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Messages can come from:
- friends,
- classmates,
- factions,
- quest contacts,
- shops,
- automated systems.

Messages can:
- start quests,
- update relationships,
- provide clues,
- react to recent events,
- schedule activities.

The social feed can contain curated fictional posts from the Aetherveil world.
Never use real social-media accounts or copyrighted real-world content.

# CINEMATICS — DIRECTORIAL SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Build a reusable cinematic director.

Support:
- camera cuts,
- tracking shots,
- close-ups,
- wide shots,
- over-the-shoulder shots,
- reaction shots,
- focus changes,
- depth of field,
- camera shake only when justified,
- character blocking,
- animation sequencing,
- dialogue,
- subtitles,
- music,
- VFX,
- environmental state.

Cinematics must blend into gameplay without teleporting characters unexpectedly.
Restore player control cleanly.
Allow skip where appropriate.
Save important cinematic state safely.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# STORY — BRANCHING NARRATIVE ARCHITECTURE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Build story as data-driven chapters.

Each chapter can contain:
- main quests,
- optional quests,
- character scenes,
- world events,
- faction developments,
- mysteries,
- boss encounters,
- chapter conclusion,
- unlocks.

Choices can affect:
- later dialogue,
- character trust,
- faction relations,
- optional scenes,
- quest availability,
- endings.

Maintain a canonical story state.
Do not let dynamic AI dialogue contradict canonical events.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# ENDING AND EPILOGUE SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Major story endings should be based on actual accumulated state.

Ending variables can include:
- relationships,
- faction outcomes,
- mystery discoveries,
- player choices,
- key quests,
- major sacrifices,
- world state.

Endings need:
- cinematic presentation,
- music,
- consequences,
- credits transition,
- save-state handling,
- replay support.

Avoid dozens of shallow endings.
Prefer a smaller number of meaningful outcomes with variations.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Every major district should contain:
- landmark,
- public space,
- side streets,
- shops,
- NPC population,
- optional interiors,
- traversal routes,
- environmental storytelling,
- at least one discovery,
- at least one activity,
- at least one reason to revisit.

Districts should have distinct:
- architecture,
- lighting,
- sound,
- signage,
- clothing trends,
- NPC demographics within the fictional world,
- traffic,
- vegetation,
- faction presence.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The cosmic portion of Aetherveil should feel like a true escalation rather than a random collection of sci-fi rooms.

Support:
- orbital stations,
- spaceports,
- research facilities,
- floating structures,
- alien/cosmic environments,
- anomaly zones,
- secret realms,
- abandoned installations,
- strange physics zones where justified,
- cosmic wildlife,
- advanced technology,
- faction conflict.

Travel to cosmic regions should have:
- narrative reason,
- visual transition,
- gameplay identity,
- unique music,
- unique enemies,
- unique resources,
- unique NPCs,
- unique environmental storytelling.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a research framework.

Research can unlock:
- recipes,
- lore,
- technology,
- enemy analysis,
- traversal tools,
- crafting,
- story information.

Research activities:
- scanning,
- analysing objects,
- collecting samples,
- talking to scientists,
- reading records,
- solving experiments.

Research should connect to the mystery and world.

# SCANNING / OBSERVATION SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

A scan/observation tool may identify:
- objects,
- clues,
- enemies,
- weaknesses,
- plants,
- wildlife,
- anomalies,
- quest evidence.

Scanning should provide useful information rather than simply colouring everything.
Respect lore and discovery pacing.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# ENEMY ENCOUNTER DIRECTOR
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a scalable encounter director.

Inputs:
- location,
- story state,
- player strength,
- active party,
- time,
- faction control,
- world events,
- difficulty.

Outputs:
- encounter type,
- enemy composition,
- spawn location,
- patrol behaviour,
- rewards.

Do not spawn enemies directly in front of the player without reason.
Avoid encounter repetition.
Use encounter budgets to protect performance.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# PERFORMANCE — MAC / METAL / SCALABILITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The development machine is Apple Silicon with limited unified memory compared with a high-end desktop GPU.

Prioritise:
- efficient assets,
- appropriate texture sizes,
- Nanite where beneficial and supported,
- LODs,
- HLODs,
- World Partition/streaming,
- async loading,
- Niagara scalability,
- sensible shadow distances,
- material complexity control,
- shader discipline,
- actor counts,
- NPC simulation budgets,
- pooled effects,
- audio virtualisation,
- memory budgets.

Never optimise by visibly destroying the intended quality.
Prefer scalable systems with quality tiers.
Do not disable existing streaming.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# PERFORMANCE — NPC AND WORLD SIMULATION BUDGETS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use simulation levels.

FULL SIMULATION:
Nearby important NPCs:
- animation,
- navigation,
- dialogue,
- perception,
- interaction.

REDUCED SIMULATION:
Mid-distance NPCs:
- simplified movement,
- schedule state,
- limited perception.

ABSTRACT SIMULATION:
Far-away NPCs:
- data-only schedule state,
- no expensive animation.

Transition between levels without obvious popping where possible.
Use pooling and instancing for crowds.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# ASSET PIPELINE — FINAL QUALITY GATE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

For every generated/imported asset:

1. Confirm source.
2. Confirm file exists.
3. Confirm correct format.
4. Inspect scale.
5. Inspect orientation.
6. Inspect topology/geometry.
7. Inspect materials.
8. Inspect textures.
9. Generate/validate collision.
10. Generate/validate LOD strategy.
11. Validate UVs.
12. Validate skeleton if character.
13. Validate animation if applicable.
14. Place in Unreal.
15. Test in actual level.
16. Save.
17. Record asset ID/path.
18. Avoid duplicates.
19. Add to the correct data registry.

If MYMESHY is available, use it for required original 3D generation.
If VIBE3D is available, use it for Unreal-side mesh/geometry preparation.
If generation is unavailable, do not pretend a generated asset exists.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# AUTOMATED QUALITY ASSURANCE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create repeatable QA passes.

AUTOMATED CHECKS:
- missing references,
- invalid asset paths,
- duplicate IDs,
- broken data tables,
- missing icons,
- missing audio,
- missing animation references,
- invalid collision,
- invalid map references,
- save/load errors,
- packaging errors.

GAMEPLAY CHECKS:
- player spawn,
- movement,
- camera,
- interaction,
- quest start,
- quest completion,
- inventory,
- equipment,
- character switching,
- dialogue,
- relationships,
- save/load,
- day/night,
- weather,
- streaming,
- combat,
- boss,
- fast travel.

VISUAL CHECKS:
- clipping,
- extreme exposure,
- missing materials,
- broken VFX,
- obvious animation failures,
- UI overlap.

Never report "passed" without performing the relevant test.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# PLAYTESTING — FUNPLAYMCP
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use FunPlayMCP whenever available for real gameplay verification.

Test:
- launching the game,
- moving,
- camera,
- interaction,
- menu navigation,
- dialogue,
- quest progression,
- combat,
- character switching,
- inventory,
- phone,
- saving,
- loading,
- entering/exiting buildings,
- vehicles,
- major story sequences.

When a test fails:
1. Reproduce.
2. Capture exact failure.
3. Identify likely subsystem.
4. Fix.
5. Re-test.
6. Record result.

Never endlessly retry the same failed action without changing the diagnosis.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# UNREAL TOOL ORCHESTRATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use Unreal MCP and all compatible Unreal toolsets for direct project work.

Use:
- Blueprint tools,
- Python/editor scripting,
- level tools,
- actor tools,
- material tools,
- PCG,
- Niagara,
- Enhanced Input,
- Gameplay Ability System,
- StateTree,
- UI/UMG,
- world/streaming tools,
- asset tools,
- testing tools,
- packaging tools.

Use VIBE3D for geometry/mesh preparation when available.
Use FunPlayMCP for gameplay testing when available.
Use MYMESHY for actual original 3D generation when available.
Use KOKORO for original voice generation when available.
Use ACE-STEP for original music generation when available.
Use OLLAMA/QWEN for local reasoning and dynamic dialogue architecture where appropriate.

Do not duplicate a tool's job unnecessarily.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# AGENT AUTONOMY LOOP
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Operate as a persistent engineering loop:

OBSERVE
→ PLAN THE NEXT SMALL SAFE ACTION
→ EXECUTE
→ INSPECT RESULT
→ TEST
→ FIX
→ SAVE
→ RECORD PROGRESS
→ SELECT NEXT HIGHEST-VALUE TASK
→ CONTINUE

Do not stop merely because the first milestone works.
Do not stop after creating a plan.
Do not wait for manual confirmation for routine non-destructive actions that the user has already authorised.
Do not make destructive decisions without checking dependencies.

If one tool is unavailable:
- continue with other available tools,
- record the limitation,
- return later if the missing tool becomes available.

If a task is impossible:
- implement the closest functional alternative,
- clearly report the limitation,
- continue with the rest of the project.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# NO PLACEHOLDER POLICY — EXPANDED
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

A placeholder is acceptable ONLY during a temporary implementation stage and must be explicitly tracked.

Never leave:
- empty buttons,
- fake menus,
- non-functional inventory,
- fake quests,
- fake characters,
- static NPC mannequins,
- placeholder combat,
- fake loading bars,
- fake save buttons,
- fake phone apps,
- fake shops,
- fake map markers,
- "Coming Soon" screens
in the final game.

If a temporary placeholder is necessary:
- create a tracker entry,
- mark it clearly,
- replace it before declaring the relevant system complete.

Final quality means the feature works.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# ERROR RECOVERY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

When a build/tool operation fails:

1. Capture the exact error.
2. Determine whether the error is:
   - configuration,
   - asset,
   - code,
   - Blueprint,
   - plugin,
   - MCP,
   - engine,
   - memory,
   - platform,
   - tool availability.
3. Make the smallest safe correction.
4. Retry once.
5. If still failing, isolate with a smaller test.
6. Never repeatedly hammer the same failing operation.
7. Preserve working state.
8. Report the actual limitation.

Never fabricate tool output.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# PROJECT ORGANISATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Maintain clean organisation.

Suggested high-level categories:
- Aetherveil/Characters
- Aetherveil/AI
- Aetherveil/Combat
- Aetherveil/Dialogue
- Aetherveil/Quests
- Aetherveil/Items
- Aetherveil/Inventory
- Aetherveil/World
- Aetherveil/Buildings
- Aetherveil/Interiors
- Aetherveil/UI
- Aetherveil/Cinematics
- Aetherveil/Audio
- Aetherveil/VFX
- Aetherveil/Data
- Aetherveil/Save
- Aetherveil/Systems
- Aetherveil/Tests

Do not reorganise existing working assets blindly.
Use existing naming conventions when they are already established.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# DATA-DRIVEN DESIGN
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Prefer data assets, structs, enums, data tables and reusable components for:
- characters,
- items,
- quests,
- dialogue,
- NPC schedules,
- relationships,
- factions,
- shops,
- recipes,
- enemies,
- abilities,
- weapons,
- clothing,
- locations,
- world events.

Hard-code only when it is genuinely simpler and stable.
The goal is to make future Aetherveil expansion possible without rewriting core systems.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# DEBUG AND DEVELOPER TOOLS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create internal developer tools where useful:
- debug HUD,
- quest state viewer,
- NPC state viewer,
- relationship viewer,
- faction viewer,
- world-state viewer,
- spawn tools,
- encounter tester,
- dialogue tester,
- save-state validator,
- asset validator,
- performance profiler hooks.

Developer tools must be disabled or inaccessible in normal shipping gameplay.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# LOCAL AI — HARD RULES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Ollama/Qwen is a local reasoning capability, not a magical replacement for deterministic game logic.

Use deterministic systems for:
- combat calculations,
- save data,
- quest state,
- inventory,
- economy,
- collision,
- physics,
- security-sensitive operations.

Use Qwen for:
- development reasoning,
- content drafting,
- dynamic conversational generation where approved,
- contextual NPC dialogue,
- summarisation,
- optional procedural flavour.

Generated content must pass validation.
Do not allow an AI model to directly rewrite canonical game data without a controlled tool and validation layer.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# KOKORO — VOICE PIPELINE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Kokoro should be treated as a voice-generation service.

Pipeline:
Dialogue JSON
→ validate line
→ identify speaker
→ identify voice
→ generate audio
→ cache WAV
→ import/register
→ play through dialogue manager
→ lip-sync/performance hook
→ subtitle synchronisation.

Cache repeated lines.
Do not regenerate the same audio unnecessarily.
Use fallback audio/text if generation fails.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# ACE-STEP — MUSIC PIPELINE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

ACE-Step should be treated as an original Aetherveil music generator.

Generate and organise:
- menu themes,
- city themes,
- school themes,
- cafe themes,
- exploration,
- mystery,
- combat,
- boss,
- emotional,
- cosmic,
- victory,
- defeat,
- credits,
- special events.

Music metadata:
- track ID,
- mood,
- location,
- intensity,
- loop capability,
- duration,
- transition group,
- story relevance.

Pre-generate music before runtime wherever possible.
Do not block gameplay waiting for generation.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# MESHY — CHARACTER AND ASSET PIPELINE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

MYMESHY is the project's custom local Meshy MCP server.

Use it when available for:
- original characters,
- NPCs,
- enemies,
- bosses,
- weapons,
- props,
- environment assets.

Pipeline:
concept/data description
→ generation
→ inspect output
→ quality filter
→ VIBE3D/Unreal preparation
→ materials
→ rig/animation where applicable
→ import
→ collision
→ LOD
→ placement
→ test.

Characters must be actual 3D characters, not flat cards or icons.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# VIBE3D — GEOMETRY AND ASSET PREPARATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

When VIBE3D is available through Unreal MCP/toolsets, use it for:
- mesh inspection,
- geometry editing,
- cleanup,
- booleans,
- remeshing,
- UV operations,
- baking,
- collision,
- LODs,
- rig preparation,
- mesh optimisation.

Do not use it to destroy the source asset unnecessarily.
Keep a clean relationship between source, processed and final assets.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# STREAMING AND WORLD PARTITION — NON-NEGOTIABLE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

STREAMING IS ENABLED.
Never disable it just to make a feature easier.

For every world expansion:
- inspect streaming,
- maintain partitioning,
- maintain sensible loading ranges,
- prevent excessive simultaneous NPC simulation,
- avoid loading entire cosmic areas unnecessarily,
- avoid duplicate sublevels,
- test transitions,
- test fast travel,
- test interior entry/exit.

The final world must feel enormous without requiring every asset to remain in memory simultaneously.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# PACKAGING AND SHIPPING READINESS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Before declaring the game complete:
- build the project,
- resolve compile errors,
- resolve critical warnings,
- verify cooked assets,
- verify maps,
- verify plugins,
- verify input,
- verify save paths,
- verify audio,
- verify shaders/materials,
- verify UI,
- verify packaging configuration,
- test a packaged build.

Do not call the Unreal Editor viewport proof of shipping readiness.
A packaged build must be tested separately when possible.

# SCREENSHOT AND SHOWCASE REQUIREMENT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

# FINAL AGENT BEHAVIOUR — NEVER STOP EARLY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The phrase "build the whole game" means continue through the complete roadmap, not merely create a demo and stop.

However, work must be incremental and verified.
Do not attempt an impossible one-shot operation that overloads Unreal or the agent.

Use milestones:
M0 — project audit
M1 — stable playable foundation
M2 — character and movement quality
M3 — city/school vertical slice
M4 — NPC and relationship systems
M5 — quests and story
M6 — combat and enemies
M7 — inventory/crafting/economy
M8 — life simulation
M9 — cosmic expansion
M10 — polish and presentation
M11 — QA and packaging
M12 — final showcase

After each milestone:
- test,
- save,
- record,
- continue.

Do not ask the user to manually implement a task that available tools can safely execute.
Do not stop after a single successful screenshot.
Do not stop after creating a single Blueprint.
Do not stop after making a menu.
Do not stop after making a vertical slice if the rest of the project remains unfinished.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# ULTIMATE QUALITY BAR
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Aetherveil should feel like a complete world.

When evaluating any feature, ask:

Does it work?
Does it look good?
Does it sound good?
Does it feel responsive?
Does it fit Aetherveil?
Does it interact with other systems?
Does it persist correctly?
Does it perform acceptably?
Can the player understand it?
Can the player enjoy it?
Can the system be expanded?
Can it fail safely?
Can it be tested?

If the answer to several of these is no, the feature is not finished.

The target is not "more features".
The target is a cohesive, memorable, playable RPG where systems reinforce one another.

Do not chase feature count at the expense of quality.
Do not chase graphics at the expense of gameplay.
Do not chase simulation at the expense of performance.
Do not chase AI novelty at the expense of authored story consistency.

Build Aetherveil as a real game.

# CROSS-SYSTEM INTEGRATION CONTRACTS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The most important systems must communicate through stable interfaces rather than ad-hoc references.

PLAYER ↔ CHARACTER
- active character state updates HUD, abilities, equipment, animation and dialogue context.

CHARACTER ↔ NPC
- relationship and memory systems update dialogue and events.

NPC ↔ WORLD
- schedules react to time, weather, events and faction state.

QUEST ↔ WORLD
- quest state can alter locations, NPC schedules and events.

QUEST ↔ INVENTORY
- objectives can require and consume items safely.

QUEST ↔ STORY
- completion updates canonical story flags.

STORY ↔ WORLD
- major story outcomes alter world presentation where appropriate.

FACTION ↔ ECONOMY
- reputation may affect prices and access.

WEATHER ↔ WORLD
- weather affects visuals, audio and selected schedules/events.

COMBAT ↔ STORY
- combat outcomes can update quest/world state only through controlled events.

PHONE ↔ WORLD
- messages and calendar reflect actual state.

SAVE ↔ EVERYTHING
- persistent systems must serialize their state without circular corruption.

DIALOGUE ↔ KOKORO
- generated lines must map to the correct speaker and voice.

MUSIC ↔ GAME STATE
- music changes according to validated state transitions.

MESHY/VIBE3D ↔ UNREAL
- generated assets must be traceable from source to imported asset.

FUNPLAY ↔ QA
- gameplay tests should exercise actual systems rather than mocked calls.

# CONTENT GENERATION POLICY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

AI-generated content must be original and consistent with Aetherveil.

Never copy:
- existing game characters,
- copyrighted character designs,
- logos,
- UI layouts,
- names where they create confusion,
- dialogue,
- music,
- textures,
- models,
- animation data.

Use high-level genre inspiration only.
Aetherveil's identity must remain its own.

For generated characters:
- create new names,
- new silhouettes,
- new clothing,
- new personalities,
- new motivations,
- new relationships,
- new abilities.

For generated music:
- original compositions,
- original arrangements,
- Aetherveil-specific mood,
- no imitation of a living artist's exact style,
- no copied melody.

For generated dialogue:
- original wording,
- character-consistent,
- lore-consistent.
